utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If I could remind you of the affirmation you took at the beginning of your evidence which still applies. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vilicic, yesterday we discussed firing from the firing position VP-1 at C-3, C-4, C-5 targets. Now, can we focus on VP-3. Can you please explain briefly your analysis of dispersion while firing from VP-3 at C-3. Let us begin there.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this slide, we see the firing position VP-3 which is firing at the firing position C-3. That is, the mortar group in Bogosica Park. On the next slide, we can see that only at the initial stage while simple preparation of data is being made, only part, or rather the whole of the Old Town was covered. However, after the correction of firing, the hits targeted the surrounding of Bogosica Park which is very far away from the Old Town. Under such conditions, if we have a precise range, they will not fall within the Old Town. However, if there is a wind, as I mentioned yesterday, a number of projectiles may fall within this zone here. That is to say, that the whole picture or pattern here will be moved in a translatory manner with respect to the firing direction. That means that some of the projectiles would hit the green zones. A general conclusion would be that provided we have defined the precise firing range, in none of these cases, a projectile fired from VP-3 of 82-millimetre mortar would fall within the Old Town. However, if there was a mistake in the estimate of the range, then some of the projectiles may have fallen in to the northern part of the Old Town. That means that if there was an error in the estimate of range, the so-called shortfall, then some of the projectiles may have landed into the northern part of the Old Town in the zone above and around the Stradun street. I'm pointing now at Stradun. So they would hit this northern part of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, this graph that we are looking at now, in the English version of your report, where can we find it?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's figure --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is that on page 59?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the first figure that I've shown. That's figure 4.10 on page 59 in the English version. And without these green and red areas, the next picture on page 60, 4.01 -- 4.101, as I said, this yellow rectangle, this dot here corresponds to this dot in figure 4.101. That is the right-hand angle of this rectangle in terms of distance from the Old Town corresponds to this rectangle in the figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vilicic. Can we please now move to VP-3, and let us hear your analysis with regard to C-4 target.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the following diagram, you can see this blue line which signifies the azimuth direction of firing at C-4 targets. During firing, we can see in figure 4.11 on page 61, well, we can see that in the course of an abbreviated preparation as opposed to what we heard earlier when we made a simple preparation, and under harsher conditions dictating better definition of initial element and lower margin of error, we can see that part of the Old Town is covered by the dispersion pattern of initial elements determined in abbreviated preparation process. As I said yesterday, when determining and correcting procedure, a number of projectile would certainly fall inside the Old Town. The next diagram shows this yellow rectangle which signifies dispersion of projectiles after the corrections and after we have accurately determined the range which indicates that unfortunately again, quite a big portion of the Old Town, from Stradun and the gate at Ploce, would be covered, which means that during regular firing at C-4, quite a few projectiles would fall inside the Old Town. This becomes even more complex if some of the projectiles were exposed to gusts of wind called Bura. We have taken the wind velocity to be 10 metres per second. And just so that you get an idea about that, when we have a wind blowing 10 metres per second, the range is increased by 150 metres. If we assume that that was the velocity of the wind, then the projectiles would fall within this 150-metre zone. But as I said, they were not able to determine the actual ballistic wind which can be five times higher in upper layers as opposed to the ground wind. Then most of the time, the trajectory would be above 300 metres, and this overshoot or deviation from firing can even be several hundred metres. We have analysed this best-case scenario when the ground wind was - which it never actually happens - was equal to the velocity of the wind in the upper layers, and that is the ballistic wind was actually only 10 metres per second. That is the best possible scenario in order to have the fewest number of projectiles hitting the Old Town. If the projectiles were exposed to lateral wind, then the projectiles as you could have seen from all these previous cases would fall lower. That means that they would fall in the more southern portion. And this cumulative corresponds to the pattern, or rather the figure on page 62 marked 4.111. You can see that the major portion of the northern part of the town was covered, which means that in this case as well, a considerable number of projectiles, while regularly firing at C-4 target, would fall into the Old Town of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vilicic, can you please --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not provide a magnified image, but I think you can see that this northeastern part of Dubrovnik was subjected to a probability or possibility of 82-millimetre shells falling inside it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When firing from VP-3 to C-4, can you tell us or just rather clarify your expert report, pages 63 and 64, what these diagrams show exactly.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said at the beginning when I showed the results of the firing from VP-3 at C-4, my primary concern was an estimate that there was actually ample time for abbreviated preparations, which means the fewer projectiles were supposed to hit the Old Town. Figure 4.12 and 4.21 indicated the situation when there was not enough time for abbreviated preparations, but rather the initial firing followed simple preparation. So the highest probability was in a reality of that being done after the command failed to provide support from 130-millimetre guns, it was only to be expected that the battalion commander try with his mortars to neutralise the Croatian mortars. However, unfortunately as you know, that had adverse effects under such weather conditions, and it provided a good chance for very many projectiles hitting the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, can we now analyse the dispersion pattern from VP-3 targeting the C-5.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is shown in the next slide, the azimuth of firing is signified by this blue line --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness just made a statement concerning the use of 130-millimetre, of the failure to use 130-millimetre guns and the effect on the Old Town as a result of that failure. That does not appear within his report. Further there is no evidence that 130-millimetre mortars were ever asked to fire at any targets in the vicinity of the Old Town. Rather, as you recall those were asked to fire out in the Lapad area and those were asked to fire out in the area of the Libertas Hotel. So I move to strike that as being not only outside of the expertise of the witness, it's outside of the information of this witness, and it's outside of the evidence of this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, allow me to explain. As my colleague certainly knows, this is a person who is an artillery expert. There is not a better person that the Defence can question about all aspects of using artillery and mortars at the time and place that we are discussing here. In addition to that, my learned friend can look at the second part of the expert analysis and the first part, the introductory part where this particular artillery piece is analysed, where it's characteristics are presented, and where its use or the absence of its use are discussed in a specific situation. I can actually give you the pages concerned, but that is in parts 1 and 2 of our expert analysis. You will find there the fact that the weapon was not used first and foremost. And secondly, you will find the characteristics of this weapon. So I don't see anything more logical but to ask the expert witness to give his views on this. After all, this is an expert, an expert witness who gives his expert opinion. And of course, the Honourable Trial Chamber will assess the facts that are in evidence, including expert opinions, and they are ultimately going to rule on all these matters. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Each of you are partly correct; each of you partly not correct in your submissions. Clearly, the witness has the expertise to indicate that 130-millimetre Howitzers are more accurate if that is the case in their firing in this situation. So that were the Howitzers to be fired, he would expect that their shells would fall with less dispersion than the 120-millimetre mortars. That is his expertise. He is going on, though, beyond that by commenting on the factual evidence to say because command didn't allow 130-millimetre Howitzers to fire, the consequences for Dubrovnik were this and that. In that respect, Mr. Weiner's submission is correct. That step is something which this Chamber must make if the factual foundations are established in the evidence and if we draw upon the expertise of this witness. So his evidence properly goes only to, in his opinion, whether one weapon is better, more accurate, more reliable in these circumstances than the other. Beyond that, his evidence is not expert evidence and is slipping into our position as triers of fact and would not be admitted to that extent. Thank you, gentlemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, we started --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just ask the Honourable Trial Chamber to say something. I agree -- do you allow me, Your Honour, to say a few words, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Vilicic, that we are going to proceed much more quickly if you simply listen to the questions put to you by Mr. Petrovic and simply answer those. I know that you have an enormous knowledge and you'd like to share with all of us, but Mr. Petrovic knows the points that are important to the case, and he will direct you to those, and if you'd confine your evidence to that, we will move more quickly. We are limited in time. We must get to the issues that are important, and only those, in the time we have. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, please let us look at VP-3 targeting C-5.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this slide -- or rather, on the preceding slide, we showed the basic azimuth at the piece which is 100 metres to the north of the Old Town of Dubrovnik. On this slide now, in order to speed matters up, we can see the dispersion of projectiles after the correction was carried out, as I've already said, on the assumption that the range was established correctly. This clearly shows that without the effect of the wind, a considerable number of projectiles are going to fall into the northern part of the Old Town. Of course, now under the influence of the wind, the dispersion would go outside the Old Town if there is a longitudinal wind. And if it were a lateral wind, then most of the area of the Old Town would have shells falling into it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where is all of this in your expertise?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is in the second part of the expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Page 82?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, page 82. It is figure 22.1 on page 82. As I've been explaining all the time, an adequate figure would be 22.11 on page 84. That would correspond to the slide we're looking at now. It's enlarged here, so there's a bit of imprecision. This can be seen here to the north of the green rectangle. We can see that the part of the Old Town of Dubrovnik above Stradun is exposed to the fall of projectiles if they do fall into the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that we have fully dealt with VP-3 now and its dispersion patterns.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So now can we move on to VP-4.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: VP-4 -- I'm sorry. I just have to say that I gave a survey here if C-6 is targeted, C-6.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: We'll get to that, please. Or rather, I'm sorry. Let's do it this way. Can I ask you while we are still dealing with VP-3, can we deal with C-6 as well, and then please tell us why you find it relevant. What does it actually constitute?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we analyse the dispersion of projectiles around C-3, C-4, and C-5, that is to say positions that two, three hundred metres away from the Old Town, C-3, and C-4 is 200 metres away from the Old Town, and C-5 is 100 metres north of the Old Town, we now wanted to see what positions could be there, that is to say, at a particular distance from the Old Town, those that do not imperil the Old Town. That is to say, which positions do not mean that the Old Town will be shelled as well. So we looked at this street, Put JNA which is 500 metres to the west of the Old Town. That's here, C-6. It is 500 metres away from the Old Town. So we analysed this, and we wanted to see what the situation was. First of all, is it simple preparation that was carried out? We see that the probability is very low for having any projectile fall into the Old Town, especially if correction is carried out. We see that this is at a considerable distance from the Old Town. So on the basis of that, we came to the conclusion that there was no need to analyse this particular firing position any longer. We came to the conclusion that as opposed to firing positions that were at 100, 200 or 300 or 350 metres away from the Old Town, a firing position that would be 500 metres away from the Old Town would not imperil the Old Town. That is to say, when there is a counterattack, then -- when there is counterbattery fire, then there would be no shells falling into the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly that your conclusion is that the minimal safe distance from the positions of the Croatian side --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll rephrase, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you'd do that, Mr. Petrovic. I understand you were trying to summarise, but I think you were slipping into some of your own evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, what is the minimal safe distance between the Old Town and the firing position of the Croatian side which would not imperil the Old Town on the basis of the conclusions of your analysis?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minimal distance of Croatian firing positions in relation to the Old Town has to be 500 metres at minimum in order not to imperil the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vilicic. I think that we can now move on to firing position VP-4.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The firing position VP-4 is Strincijera. Mortars of 82 millimetres. This mortar in this position are characteristic in terms of the following: There were six 82-millimetre mortars there according to the information provided by Zeljko Soldo specifically. And from that firing position, we analysed the firing at the first objective, that is C-4, of the Croatian mortar to the east of the Old Town 200 metres away, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And what are the results that you obtained in terms of the dispersion pattern?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the following slide, what is depicted is the dispersion pattern when there is abbreviated preparation, and also after the correction. It can be seen that in the initial stage, there is a chance of having some shells fall into the Old Town. However, once correction is carried out, in normal conditions without any effect coming from the wind, projectiles would fall outside the Old Town. Perhaps a projectile could hit Revelin or rather Star Revelin, the fort of Revelin. On the next side, we see what we have looked at until now as well, that is to say when the projectile is exposed to a lateral wind or another wind, again projectiles would fall into the Old Town to a very small degree, except the initial stage. So that is C-4.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: All right. In relation to this firing position, could you show us the appropriate page in the expert analysis where we can find the graphs that pertain to this firing position.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Practically, we did not provide these diagrams in the analysis here because our conclusion was that practically shells could not fall into the Old Town when dealing with C-5.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, we are talking about VP-4 firing at C-4.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I beg your pardon. Please look at page 66 then and 67.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So that's it?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, page 66, figure 4.17. So we're talking about pages 66 and 67, figure 4.171 is on page 67. In view of the situation here, I did not prepare slides for these particular pages, that is to say, pages 68 and 69 when the same target is engaged, but on the assumption that simple preparation was carried out. First of all, again, it is a very small number of projectiles that could perhaps hit Revelin in the stage of preparation or rather correction. So that's why we did not show it. I'm sorry about this slip of the tongue. C-5 appeared on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, I would now like to ask you to interpret firing from VP-4 at C-5. If I'm not mistaken, that is in the second addendum attached to your expert analysis.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These diagrams are at the very end in the annex, in annex 25, that is, in the addendum to the expert analysis. These are sketches 23, 23.1, and 23.21. On this diagram, we see that once fire correction has been carried out in terms of targeting a weapon that is 100 metres to the north of the Old Town, a considerable part of this central and northern part of the town would be exposed to projectiles falling before correction was carried out. Afterwards, once correction is carried out, then this northern part, so it would be the Broketa and St. Barbara towers, that is what would be affected, that is to say to the north of the Stradun. Individual shells could fall there in that case. Of course, now under the influence of the wind, projectiles would fall further into the Old Town. And to the west, this is a pattern that is the result of this, and that is shown on figure 23.11. So we're talking about the yellow rectangle, and it would move a bit to this side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vilicic. I hope that this exhausts --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We show on the next slide what this looks like when it's enlarged, so we see that it is to the north of Stradun. That is what is affected in this area here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now that we've analysed all the relevant firing positions from the JNA side and all the relevant targets, potential targets, on the Croatian side, I would like to ask you to give a summary conclusion. First of all, I would ask you what is the minimal distance or minimal position if we're talking about Croatian positions, that ensures the safety of the Old Town and that the Old Town would not be touched at all? This is to say on the basis of the conclusions of your analysis?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have been saying showing you the results of potential targeting of C-6 target, which we show to be at 500 metres north of the Old Town, the first conclusion is that the distance of Croatian firing positions, artillery positions, should have been not less than 500 metres away from the Old Town. Any distance closer to the Old Town than that would inevitably lead to certain projectiles falling within the Old Town during counterbattery fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, may I ask you to focus on the following questions: What is your total estimate of the effect of mortars from VP-3, VP-4, and VP-5 firing positions in this part of your expert report?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my expert report I gave a complete conclusion after analysing all these options. I gave a conclusion on the effect of mortar fire from VP-3, VP-4, and VP-5 firing positions if they would target C-3, C-4, and C-5 situated around the Old Town of Dubrovnik. My main conclusion based on the calculations performed and the analysis, that the disposition of Croatian firing positions was such that it led to a certain number of projectiles falling within the Old Town of Dubrovnik. However, one must bear in mind that this was further aggravated by an extremely bad meteorological situation on that 6th of December, an extremely strong Bura wind --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The counsel asked the witness the following question: "What is your total estimate of the effect of mortars 3, 4, and 5 firing positions in this part of your expert report?" And he asked him about the total number of shells falling into the Old Town. And now we're talking about the weather, the Croatian positions. That's not answering the question. If you look at the two questions --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, I would like to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, if you want to ask different questions, do that. But we will judge the relevance by the question. So what is essentially happening at the moment is the witness is roaming over a wide field of matters that aren't related to your questions. So if you would be more specific in your questions, and the evidence will be more controlled. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you allow me to state my opinion what this expert witness wishes to do is to give a conclusion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I've given you a ruling. I think you can proceed to lead your relevant evidence. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, just tell us where in your expert report can we find the conclusions relating to the overall firing activity of VP-1, VP-3, and VP-4 mortars?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the English version on page 88, you can find conclusions on the firing activity of mortars from VP-1, VP-3, and VP-4 positions, and their effect on the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like us to go over a certain number of other questions that I have listed and that you as an expert are qualified to answer. First of all, is it possible to use mortars mounted on vehicles and under what conditions?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There are several solutions available in the world involving the mounting of mortars on vehicles of medium capacity without particular reconstruction of vehicles being necessary. It is necessary to use an all-surface, four-wheel-drive vehicle. Such solutions exist in all armies. We also had prototypes for such mounted mortars. Every mortar can rather simply be mounted on a vehicle and fire. It is enough to put a mortar on a base plate, and I have to tell this Honourable Court that I was one of the team of the designers of the M-69A mortar. You put sandbags and put a special base underneath that is designed so as to disperse the burden to all sides. You can use charges 1, 2, 3 and fire from this mortar without any problem. In the specific case of Dubrovnik, the third charge in terms of range is quite sufficient to target or rather to cover the firing lines held by the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us briefly, is it possible to use mortars from a concrete or stone surface?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same applies as to vehicle-mounted mortars. Mortars can fire from a concrete surface provided that it is prepared in the way that I described. And one can also put it on specially prepared terrain. You can put sandbags and arrange stones around, and then put the base plate on the sandbags. And with smaller charges, you can use the mortar in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it possible to fire with either artillery weapons or mortars without aiming devices, without optical sights? That is my first question. And if that is possible, what would be the precision of such firing without aiming?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I don't think that's covered in his report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't know the answer to that, Mr. Weiner. Mr. Petrovic, can you assist us. Is this set out in the report?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the precision of firing activity of both sides is covered in the report, the precision of firing. The first next logical question is what the effect of absence or presence of optical sights would be on the precision of using these weapons. That issue has already been considered. Remember Witness Negodic who testified that he had opened fire without aiming devices. We now brought an expert artillery witness to clarify this issue. If my learned friends will continue with this approach, we would be totally unable to explore certain very important matters for our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner isn't suggesting it's not relevant, Mr. Petrovic; he's suggesting that this is an expert witness. The Rules provide for disclosure of their opinions to the other side before, and he says that this matter is not the subject of disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it was not disclosed in this way, but I hope that elementary logic should have led my learned friend to the conclusion that issues concerning artillery, the use of artillery and artillery pieces is precisely the thing that we are going to be discussing with this expert witness. We cannot emphasise every sentence and every comma and disclose in advance that we are going to discuss it. It is a formalist approach that is totally hamstringing us in our work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't think that observation is entirely justified, Mr. Petrovic. It requires more care on your part. But let me say to you that the Chamber's view is that this is a matter which is so alive on the evidence that it would be of value to have the opinion on this rather obvious issue so that despite the failure to comply with disclosure, in the discretion of the Chamber you may lead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I thank you again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, could you please answer this question that I just asked.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Firing from mortars without aiming devices is impermissible because after discharge of every shell, the mortar changes both direction and elevation. The barrel changes both range and elevation which means if we do not have a properly rectified aiming device which means that if you look at a certain point in a distance and the barrel is trained in that direction at that point, we cannot expect that the next projectile will follow this same trajectory because with every discharge, the initial angle will be the same due to the bounce. Without an aiming device, we have a greater dispersion both in terms of range and deflection. If you draw a mechanical line across the barrel, you will have a basic aiming device, or you could possibly use a quadrant with an angle gauge. Without using even that, there is no chance of precise aiming.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vilicic. Did you have an opportunity to read the report of an artillery expert who testified earlier in this case as a Prosecution witness?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you briefly in a couple of sentences tell us if you are familiar with his conclusions and how you view the conclusions of the Prosecution expert.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did have this opportunity. I read it. I analysed it. And I also had the opportunity of hearing the witness testifying in this courtroom. First and foremost, he based his entire report on the probable dispersions according to table values, which cannot be applicable in this case. It cannot be precise. He did not take into account the mountainous characteristics of the terrain where the actual firing took place. He did not take into account the rear-sloping terrain. He did not take into account the positions of the other side, some of which were as close as 100 metres from the Old Town. His conclusions, in fact, the values he quotes in his report fall about 50 per cent short of the actual values.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you show us that.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be useful if I could use the overhead projector. May I explain now?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this first table, we considered the first case in the annex, firing position of the Zarkovica mortar targeting the C-4 target near Ploce. The Prosecution expert gave the following results for the third, fourth, and fifth charges. He said they were semi-ellipses on the order of magnitude of 112 by 80. According to all rules of the theory of firing, because I also taught at the military academy, this expert witness Poje Jozef also attended the academy and should have heard this, when firing the primary weapon and in determining the initial firing data, the pattern of dispersion has the following values: 667 by 536, not 112 by 80. After correction of fire in using four pieces, the realistic pattern of dispersion has the following values: 230 by 165. On average, Mr. Poje presented to this Court results that fall about 51.3 per cent short of the real actual dispersion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please go on.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the next slide, we see the next case considered by Mr. Jozef Poje, that is when 120-millimetre mortars are targeting a target north of the Old Town, near Ploce. You see that his ellipse of dispersion is 280 by 152, whereas the realistic ellipse is 577 by 423. Again, his pattern of dispersion is 51.5 per cent less than the real dispersion that you get after performing the correction of firing in concentrated targeting of the same target by a mortar platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where can we find this in your expert report?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not attach that to my report. But when I came here, I presented to you, and I hope that you made it known in advance that I would also be analysing the results obtained by the Prosecution expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: These two tables that you just discussed --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are in the documents. The first document provided by the Prosecution to you on the 1st of April, that's the first document. And the second is the annex submitted on the 15th of May 2004. Those are the two documents that we analysed and that you made available to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vilicic. Just two more short questions: Yesterday, we discussed the firing position VP-2, and you testified based on the information that you had available and that were included as evidence before this Honourable Chamber is that at this VP-2 position, there were two 76-millimetre firing pieces, the so-called ZIS. My question is when firing directly at Srdj from VP-2, from the ZIS 76-millimetre firing piece, is it possible that under such circumstances when Srdj is targeted directly and probably missed, the projectile fired from this particular weapon fall into the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before the witness replies to this question, I would like to distribute to this Honourable Chamber two documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, could you please answer the question, if you can.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The VP-2 position in the Vrastica sector, there were three M-42 guns. You can see on the monitor the slide indicating the VP-2 firing position in the Vrastica sector where three anti-armour 76-millimetre M-42 ZIS guns were. And the azimuth of firing direction showed on the slide shows the Srdj fortress marked by C-1. It is clear from this slide that this direction completely deviates by several tens degrees, or translated into other measures, several hundred thousandths [as interpreted] parts from the original direction. On the next slide, you can see the trajectory of the projectile 76 millimetre which indicates the variation in the elevation of the terrain, the Old Town is at approximately 4.750 metres, the Srdj is at elevation 403, and the Vrastica firing position of the guns is at 390 metres elevation. The height of this curve, so if we are to link these two dots, the difference between these two points is only 88 millimetres. That means that this trajectory is extremely flat, but it corresponds to this type of weapon, which is an anti-armour weapon intended for targeting vehicles and bunkers. This trajectory corresponds exactly to the table values which show that while firing at the Srdj fortress and under the assumption that it had been missed, the projectile would continue to fly, and it will fall at 5.5 kilometres from the firing position. In other words, even if the Old Town had been at the same direction with Srdj and from the previous slide we can clearly see the difference between the direction leading to the flight of the projectile over the Old Town, therefore the centre of the Old Town is 5.000 metres from this point, and the projectile would fall at a distance of 5.400 metres. In other words, if they had fired at the Old Town itself by targeting elements relevant for Srdj, the projectile would overshoot and fall into the sea. So there is not even a theoretical change that whilst targeting Srdj that the projectile would fall inside the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please just show us, because we were not able to see this second sketch. Could you please explain to us what we can see in that sketch.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This image or this drawing shows what I just explained, that they had taken the wrong direction by using a derectified sight. The projectile would fly over the Old Town and fall here, which is at 5.500 metres from this 76-millimetre gun. Presuming that they missed the Srdj fortress by a couple of tens of metres and that it overshot the Srdj fortress, then the projectile would miss the target, or rather miss the Old Town by 1.500 metres to the west. Therefore, there is no chance that while targeting the imperial fortress that any projectile would fall into the Old Town that had been fired from the firing position at Vrastica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vilicic. Could you please tell us, after reviewing the video documents that you had at your disposal while compiling your expert report, were you able to go through and see this video documentation?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And in the expert analysis we dedicated a special chapter, that is Chapter 8 on page 94 onwards, we analysed the results of the initially supplied data referring to the damage inflicted inside the Old Town of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the video material that you had reviewed, and by that I'm referring to two video footage that are in the case file, which is P78 and P145, from these videos, did you notice anything characteristic that would be relevant to be presented to this Honourable Chamber?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say that while preparing for presenting the results contained in my report, we very carefully viewed the videos provided by the Tribunal, that is, the videotapes that we had received, the film showed here which was shot by Mr. Jusic, and we also viewed the CD recording made on the 8th of December while members of the Yugoslav Army visited the site and established the level of damage inside the Old Town of Dubrovnik. After carefully reviewing the first video made and presented by Mr. Jusic in this Chamber --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can we just have a look at this particular piece of footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will first show you from this video a segment of the videotape. Just a moment, please, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I indicate, Mr. Petrovic, it would be helpful if we can know the point on the exhibit that this --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that's Exhibit P78 from the 19th minute and 17 seconds until 19 minutes and 28 seconds. And Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond then Exhibit P145, the 58th second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the beginning of the videotape marked V0002732 presented by Mr. Jusic in this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please just show the particular segment.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now we are going to go to the 19th minute of this video. And from the 19th minute and 14 seconds, this is the picture of Stradun. We can see this dog running around. Then the camera goes to the left, and now I will just rewind a little. I will show you this particular frame. You can see this dog running away from Stradun. And now we have frozen the frame here. Here, this is the St. Blaise's church. One projectile had fallen here. It has pushed the debris backwards. And after analysing this picture and based on our experience and knowledge, we concluded that this projectile probably came from west, not from the east. So we have taken out this frame and converted into another software package in order to be able to freeze this frame and analyse it properly. I apologise. I will just have to shift now to a different software, Quicktime movie, so we can follow it. You can see it now on your screens. So by shifting this slowly, I can move the image, so this is the dog that I drew your attention to, the dog that is running. So the camera is moving to the left. And now, here we come to this detail that I said that we had analysed. And based on the fact that when a shell falls under a certain angle, the impact wave and the explosion of the shell, the part which is facing the ground, is affecting the ground and is pushing the debris from the contact point, from the hole that the projectile had made. And the contact wave that has a reverse effect, it scatters the pieces of the shell that can fly around. And depending if they face or come into any obstacle or perhaps persons, can cause damage. We also notice, which we are going to see in another video, that this balcony, balustrade had been damaged. This is the balcony in front of the church and these columns here have been damaged. So our conclusion was that the shell fell under such an angle that creates an angle towards the western part, and that is a considerable angle which makes it possible for these debris pieces to fly around and that they, in fact, damaged these parts here. Still, at the time, we were unable to definitively conclude whether we were completely right or not. However, after we had viewed the second video, at its very beginning --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are talking now about the P145 exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's another video.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've just explained what we are discussing. Could you please just continue.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see the damage here and the crater that was created here. I'm sorry. We could not show -- well, I've stopped it here. You see this crater. The material was thrown out towards the back. You can see that it was filmed on the 8th of December 1991. We saw now definitely that the projectile pierced the stone surface, damaged in a semi-circular fashion this stone, and that these parts were thrown out here. On this basis, we corroborated our assumption this projectile came from the west; that is, from the west in relation to the Old Town and fell here in front of the church of St. Blaise. This could not have been a projectile that came from the east.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vilicic. Now, since we've dealt with this last subject, I would like to ask you very briefly to give us the general conclusion of your expert analysis, the one you did at the request of the Defence of General Pavle Strugar.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would just like to present to the Honourable Trial Chamber our general conclusion now. In the English version, a broad conclusion is on page 97. And the final conclusion is on page 99. If you allow me, I would just like to say a few words. Our basic conclusion, and everything that I've said so far points to the following: First of all, that the distribution of firing positions of the Croatian forces that were at distances that were less than 500 metres away from the Old Town in terms of counterattacks, it imperilled the Old Town. On that basis, we drew the conclusion that even without intentionally targeting the Old Town, projectiles fall into it. In other words, the positions of the Croatian forces led to the fact that a number of projectiles landed in the Old Town. I must say that firing positions of artillery pieces of the Yugoslav People's Army that were in the area of Ledenice, mortars that were 120-millimetre mortars, 82 millimetres at Strincijera, and the others at the area of Dubac were at a relatively large distance. That is to say, relatively within the range of these two firing positions, in terms of their maximum range. Which obviously points to the fact that these mortars were positioned against all the rules. Allow me to say this. I was a colonel of the Yugoslav People's Army. I have been retired since the 1st of January 1994. It is obvious there was a battalion there. A battalion was at the location that corresponds to that of a battalion that is on the defence. Since they were where they were, they were there to give fire support in terms of defence, not in case of attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I would object to this, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It is stated within his report, he makes similar findings. However, this gentleman is here as a ballistician. He is not here as a command and control expert. He is not here as a military strategist. He's not here as a military tactical expert. This is outside his area of expertise, and should not be allowed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, can we please focus on what your conclusion is, that is to say on pages 97, 98, and 99 of your expert report.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry for digressing in that way, as Mr. Weiner said. I do apologise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll go back to this now. First of all, I spoke of the distribution of the firing forces of the Croatian Army, and that is what imperilled the Old Town. Secondly, poor weather conditions contributed to a larger number of shells falling within the Old Town. As I've said, all firing positions regardless of whether they are stationary or mobile that were at a distance that is less than 500 metres from the Old Town imperil the Old Town of Dubrovnik. In the analysis, we made calculations in terms of standard requirements; namely, how many projectiles have to be fired in order to destroy C-3, C-4, and C-5. This number of shells considerably exceeds, or rather it is a couple of hundred shells. So on the basis of the calculations that we made, and on the basis of the information that we had, namely, that the mortars fired from a 120-millimetre mortar that had great destructive effect, they fired up to one combat kit, that is to say up to 160 shells. So our calculations showed that this number would have to have been much larger if the intention was to destroy these targets. If that had been the intention, so many shells would have fallen on the Old Town that it practically would have been destroyed. On the basis of all of this, our clear and unequivocal conclusion is that on the basis of the complete analysis that we carried out, it cannot be concluded that the Old Town of Dubrovnik was intentionally targeted or fired at. Had this been the case, it would have practically been destroyed as I've already said because the fall of projectiles and the localities where damage was sustained in the Old Town clearly indicate that the largest number of projectiles fell, and this is corroborated by our analysis as well, in the southern part, that is to say to the south of Stradun --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Northern part.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] North of Stradun, and also to the west. Whereas as far as the central, eastern and southern parts of Stradun are concerned, there are only individual reports of damage which clearly indicates that perhaps some projectiles could have done astray in the situation that prevailed then in view of the weather conditions. That would be our final conclusion, that is to say, of our expert analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your exhaustive and detailed analysis. Your Honour, this concludes the examination-in-chief of the expert witness by the Defence. Your Honour, first of all, I would like to give an explanation in view of the questions that you addressed to the Defence yesterday by your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. So Mr. Vilicic and the team that worked with Mr. Vilicic, when working on this expert analysis used material that was relevant and that was accessible at the time when the expert analysis was compiled. This is an analysis that is quite voluminous, very detailed, and very complex. At the time when the main part of this analysis was done, the Prosecution witness list included witnesses that you mentioned here yesterday, Your Honour. That is the reason why some of the information was taken from these sources as well. However, the Defence wishes to point out that it is their position that they are quite aware of the fact that some of these documents were not actually tendered into evidence in this case. And therefore, we wish to point out that we espouse the same approach that was adopted during the testimony of Jozef Poje, the Prosecution expert; namely, that the expert findings of Mr. Vilicic and his associates are relevant to the extent to which they correspond to the evidence existing in this case. The point of the analysis of Mr. Vilicic is confined to the evidence in this case, Your Honours. The Defence, of course, is aware of the fact that other facts that were resorted to and that are not in evidence will not be taken into account. So dispersion tables in terms of falls into the Old Town directly correspond to the evidence that was heard by this Trial Chamber over these past seven or eight months, for as long as the trial has been going on. I hope that my explanation will suffice, and I believe that this is what you had in mind when you addressed that question to us yesterday, Your Honour. Your Honour, may I also ask that the report of Dr. Vilicic, the basic report in the English version, then the Serbian version, then the annexes attached to the basic report that is, annex number II, then the curriculum vitae of Mr. Vilicic, and two graphs that were used a few minutes ago in this courtroom be admitted into evidence as Defence exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could I ask that these exhibits be held as ID exhibits until the end of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I suppose that merely repeats what happened the other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So we'll just hold it until the end of cross-examination, Mr. Petrovic. We'll see what emerges. But do I take it you would also be wanting to tender the two diagrams? Did I miss that, sorry? I was distracted by --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we will simply not mark them at all at the moment. We will wait and hear the cross-examination, and if I should forget, if you could be alert to remind me the question of admission at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In fact, you could admit those two documents. I have no objection to those, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it would be nice to put them all together in one group, the exhibits, if they become that. So we'll hold them all. Thank you very much, Mr. Petrovic, and particularly for the timeliness of your dealing with this evidence. It's obviously a convenient time now to have the first break. And we'll resume at 25 past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Dr. Vilicic.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Dr. Vilicic, towards the end of your testimony or end of your testimony, you discussed a crater in front of the St. Blaise's church in the Old Town. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And in the two videos, the two segments from the two videos, we saw that crater.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And if we look at that crater facing St. Blaise's church, we see a hole, and then some raised tiles, and then the church. Isn't that correct? I'm asking you the question. I can show you the video later. I can show it from here.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So we see the hole first, then the raised tiles, and then the church. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So that means based on your statement -- I'm sorry, the proofing notes, that the projectile was flying towards St. Blaise's church. Isn't that correct? Because you said there is the hole first, and then the raised tiles. The projectile goes down, causes the hole, and then raises the tiles. So the direction that the projectile is flying is in the direction of St. Blaise's church. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That does not have to mean that that's the direction. It fell in the direction that is in the vicinity of St. Blaise's church. It is not to say that it aimed at St. Blaise's church.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, I'm not saying it aimed at St. Blaise's church. But from the hole and the raised tiles, it was heading towards St. Blaise's church. We agree upon that, don't we, sir? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely speaking, it fell in the vicinity of the church of St. Blaise.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I understand that. But what I'm saying is the direction it was coming from, I'm not saying they targeted St. Blaise's church. But the direction it was coming from was towards St. Blaise's church. We agree upon that, don't we, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, the direction goes by the church of St. Blaise, if we want to be specific. Since the projectile fell in the immediate vicinity of the church, as it flew, the trajectory of the projectile rather, went by the church of St. Blaise. If we were to put a vertical surface this way, and if we look at the trajectory of the projectile, then this was -- the plane was next to the church of St. Blaise, this imaginary plane.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I have a piece of paper in my hand. Actually, this will be St. Blaise's church, this computer screen. The raised tiles are in front. Then the hole. So the projectile has to be coming this way towards the direction of St. Blaise's church. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The projectile came from there, from there. If this is St. Blaise's church, the plane through which the trajectory went goes like this. This is the church. It's exactly this way --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... where the --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This way. This way. It went this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, if you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The record should record that the trajectory indicated by the witness is one roughly parallel to the front face of St. Blaise's church, as I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you indicated that the fact that the hole was in the rear in this statement, the discovery that we received, sir, the fact -- you indicated the fact that the tiles are in the front, and the hole is in the back meant that it came from the back to the front. That's what your attorneys gave to us. Are you changing your opinion now? Are you changing the discovery that was supplied by your attorneys? You used east and west, but you indicated that the fact that the tiles were raised, you indicated that the projectile came towards the raised tiles. Isn't that correct? That's what this discovery says here. Are you changing that now?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not changing my opinion. Please, let me quite precise. The hole -- I mean, in relation to the hole, the bricks or tiles are raised on the eastern side, and the projectile came from the western side.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, all I want you to do is -- the hole is in front. I know, but sir, without -- the hole is in front. There's a hole in front, a U-shaped hole which you called west. Okay. You said -- that's okay. Listen to my question first. You said without talking about east or west, you said that the tiles are raised. That means because the tiles are raised, the projectile came towards the raised tiles. Isn't that correct? Without talking east and west, in the discovery you indicated -- that's correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So the fact that the tiles are raised means the projectile came towards the tiles. Since you've just said we have the church here, then the raised tiles, and then the holes in front of it, the projectile has to go towards -- in the direction of the church because you just said the projectile goes towards the raised tiles.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that depends on interpretation. I said precisely that the plane through which the projectile flew practically passes by the church. And I even drew it --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, sir, you just indicated to me three times we said you have the church, the raised tiles in front of the church, and then the hole in front of the raised tiles. And I just asked you if the projectile runs towards the raised tiles. And you said yes. Now, I'd like to show you Exhibit P13. Would you look at that, please. Sir, could P13 be placed on the ELMO. Sir, can you just show us where the north, southeast, and west is. Or let me take you through it. The witnesses so far has indicated the east is the harbour area. Isn't that correct? Correct, the east is the harbour, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the east. And over here is west. North is up. South is down. Strictly speaking, there is a certain angle if you want to be precise. There is a certain inclination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: South is down. Now, do you see the number 13 there, St. Blaise's church?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. And the projectile fell --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, sir, listen to me. You indicated in front of the church there were raised tiles, then the hole. And that the projectile came towards the raised tiles. Therefore, the projectile had to have come north to south. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you stated a few moments ago the projectile went through the raised tiles, went towards the raised tiles. The raised tiles are directly in front of number 13. So if the projectile is going in the direction of the church, that's going from north to south. Let's face it.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. That's a completely incorrect interpretation. If I can show you on this screen, look at the slabs. The stone slabs located in the Luza square are oriented south-north. And the spheric thing on the other picture --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let's go to the picture. First let's go if we could to see an overview from the back angle. P145, please, at 58 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I start the footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, we'll do it on our end, sir.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You will.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. 58 seconds, please. Right there. We see the hole in front. We're -- our backs are to the church. We see the stones that have been raised, and then we see the hole. Isn't that correct? Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay, now could we go to the other angle. Could we go to -- just a second.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, look at the direction of the slabs. The spheric --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: One moment, sir. P78, please, we'll look at it right from the front view in front of the church at 19, 25 seconds. Right after the dog. Hold on. Hold on. Actually, could we go back for a second. We're facing up the Stradun towards the west at this point. Correct? Now, we're going to turn south. Let's turn south. Can we continue south. Keep on going to 25 seconds. A little more, please. Little more. Stop. What we have in front of the church, we're facing south now. We have the hole and the raised stones. And you indicated the projectile would move towards the raised stones. Therefore, the projectile is facing south.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not correct. Please, you are interpreting this completely inaccurately. Look at how the slabs are located. Look at this material thrown backwards. Now, look at the previous film, and you will see that from the hole, the debris goes into the normal direction south-north. You are claiming it is south-north because I said it was east-west because the discharged -- the propelled material was thrown west. The slabs are oriented --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The material is thrown west. So if didn't come north to south, if the materials are thrown west. So therefore it came from the east, so either it came from the JNA in the north or it came from the JNA in the east. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the complete answer is not on the record. The answer the witness gave concerning the orientation of the slabs did not go into the record in its entirety. It is in the 21st line of page 37. I'm just asking that the witness be allowed to complete his answer concerning the orientation of the slabs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, he wasn't responding to my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very shortly, I think we will reach the point where you will allow him to give his explanation as to why he sees it differently than you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He did, but he said it was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm letting you put your proposition so far. But clearly, there is a difference between you, and it will have to emerge soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you've testified five times, I believe, now there's a hole, there are raised tiles, and then there's the church. Correct? Correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you testified now twice that the projectile moved towards the raised tiles.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So that's now three times. So if the projectile moved towards the raised tiles, it is moving towards the church. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Parallel with the church, if you insist. You keep trying to tell me that it was going towards the church. If it was heading directly towards the church, the hole would be in front of the church, not next to it. I think I will have to start speaking English so we can understand each other without mediation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If it's moving towards the church or in the direction or towards the angle to the side of the church, it's moving south. Isn't that correct? Because you're facing south if you're facing the church. That's correct, isn't it? If you're facing the church, you're facing south?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, you persistently keep trying -- yes, it's correct. Allow me to tell you, south-north is the layout of the slabs on the Luza square. They are perpendicular to the church. That's the direction in which the slabs are laid. And the orientation of the slabs is north-south. And I said the projectile came perpendicular to the direction of the slabs, which is east-west, that is, west-east. The raised slabs relative to the hole are on the east, whereas the thrown-out material faces west. And based on this thrown-out debris, I said the projectile came from east to west. The orientation -- the orientation of this hole, and you can see it on film 25.53 - I don't know it by heart - you can see that there is a spheric hole, a crater, and it is oriented towards the west. It is on the west side. And the raised tiles are on the east side. If we take that the centre of orientation is the centre of the hole.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, if the centre of the hole is the centre of orientation and the slabs are behind the hole as you've now testified six - this is now - you're nodding - seven times - then the slabs are on the south side. You've got your north, west, east, and south. So the slabs are on the south side. Correct? Not on the west or not on the east.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You keep trying to prove that the projectile came from the north. And I'm telling you based on the orientation of the slabs, which is north-south, the projectile came from the west. And if we take the centre of the hole as a reference point, north is on this side, as we can see on the screen, it is facing you. South is away from you. Right is west, and left is east. And if we face north, of course to my right would be east and my left would be west. And if we look at it on the drawing, I am looking from the north towards the south, and I'm seeing the church. And clearly, west is on the right. From the right, that is, from the west, the projectile came flying eastward and came close to the church. And we can clearly see on this second film from the orientation of the slabs that the crater was created from the west to the east. And the material was propelled, thrown out towards the east.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, if the material was propelled to the east, it would be on this side, to your left.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's a problem of interpretation. Page 40, line 12, the last word is not the one recorded. I would like that clarified, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: East. Is that the word?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If we're facing south, you see all the materials to the right of the hole. That's to the west, sir.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So all thrown --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: West, west --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: -- to the west.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it was just a misinterpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said several times the time material was thrown out towards the west. I said the first time and I'm repeating for the umpteenth time the material was thrown out to the west and the slabs are raised on the east side of the hole.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, if the hole is in front of us and the slabs are behind the hole as you said seven times now I believe, the slabs are on the south side. Do you want to maintain it's on the west, sir? If you have the hole, you have the slabs, and then you're having the church. We're facing the church. The slabs are in front of the church. The slabs have to be on the south.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, look at the film that you have just shown, and you will see. Start earlier. Start when the camera is shooting the balustrade of the church moving right and showing the hole. If you look at the hole where you see the wreath, you can see clearly that the slabs are facing north-south, and the curve of the hole is looking west. And on that detail, you can see that they are on the west.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So if the slabs are on the south -- let's say even slightly angled to the southwest, that means - you indicated the projectile was moving towards the slabs, the raised tiles I mean, when I say slabs - it has to be coming from the northeast. That's common sense, sir.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Northeast. I cannot understand how it could have come from northeast when the material was propelled westward. You are losing sight of the fact that a mortar shell, when it falls, when it lands, throws material backwards. Why? Because the impact wave hits the ground, bounces and throws all the material backwards. Whereas the other one, because it is at an inclination, throws out additional pieces; in this case, towards the church. Why is there absolutely no material on this side? Can you explain it to yourself? Why don't you see east of the hole any material, any debris? Because the impact wave discharged material on one side, and then didn't discharge any material on the other because it simply rushed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If you notice 58 and this one, the two exhibits are slightly different. Were you there on December 6th, sir, in front of the St. Blaise's church? No.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Clearly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You weren't there on December 7th.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I've seen the film.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you don't know if anyone moved any of those bricks, if anyone moved any of that rubble, if anyone swept it towards a pile, swept it away from the church? You don't know that, do you, sir, because you weren't there? Correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but one can see clearly in second 58 that nobody had shifted anything, that everything was lying exactly as on the previous film.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, before 58 was taken, you weren't there either and you don't know if anyone moved anything, do you? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't understand your question. If you said that I wasn't there either on the 5th, the 6th, or the 7th, but it is clear when you look at the film --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, sir, that's not my question.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- when you see the hole --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, all I'm saying is you weren't there on the 6th or the 7th, so you don't know if anyone tampered with the hole, if anyone cleaned the area, if anyone kicked some of those stones into the hole or just kicked them towards the hole, you don't know any of that because you weren't there. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, to me, as an expert who made an analysis of both these video films, I can only confirm that I wasn't there. But you cannot convince me that these slabs could have been moved --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, the question -- okay, that's fine. The rubble -- you don't know if anyone moved it. You just don't know because you weren't there.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the film, I see that nobody moved them because it's lying exactly as in the other film. There is an absolute similarity between 25.53 and the film of Djelo Jusic. The similarity is such that --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you went there before Djelo Jusic's film was taken? Sir, you were not there prior to Jusic's film taken, were you?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true, that I wasn't there in the region.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that was taken the day after, the day after the impact. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. On the film --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you don't know if anyone tampered with that between December 6th and December 7th, do you?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No -- yes, yes. Yes, it's true that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, are you the same Dr. Vilicic who testified in the Galic case?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you the same Dr. Vilicic who was questioned by Judge Orie about taking a photograph and changing it, turning it 180 degrees so it would then fit your conclusions because the regular view of the photograph did not fit your conclusions? Are you that same Dr. Vilicic? And it's also listed in a footnote in the Galic decision that you manipulated a piece of evidence? Are you that same Dr. Vilicic?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true. And Honourable Judge Orie, the transcript actually shows quite the opposite of what you're saying. The transcript says precisely that the photograph used there has no influence on the conclusion that the shell had come from the northern direction. And it was pure manipulation with that picture that had been placed there without any intention to prove the opposite of what was said in the Prosecution material. I think it's absolutely ridiculous. The transcript clearly shows that I confirmed that this photograph has no impact on the thesis provided me by the Tribunal, the allegation made. The Tribunal has no impact on the conclusion concerning the direction of the shell. And I can say that this interpretation of yours that I manipulated everything in order to corroborate my conclusion is totally groundless. And you can see that the conclusion is not changed one bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, let me read -- would you like me to read two pages from the transcript of the Galic trial? Pages 20.364 and 20.365. Question, Judge Orie: "Dr. Vilicic, the question is the following: If you turn a photograph 180 degrees because it becomes more logic with one version of the event, that takes away for anyone who reads the report the opportunity to notice such an inconsistency or such an illogical difference between the photograph and the version of the event. The question now is that you should do that on your own without telling those who read the report that you did it and why you did it and whether this would not be improper to do, even if you might have done it with the best intentions." Answer: "Well, this change, in my opinion, doesn't change anything in regard to the conclusions about the place where the projectile exploded and the altitude, the elevation. It doesn't change the direction from which the projectile came."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "Say the photograph is illogical in view of the version given to you of the event would it not have been proper to draw the attention to this illogic rather than turning the photograph for 180 degrees to adapt to the version of the event -- of the version that was presented to you. It might have been important to this Chamber, for example, not to believe one version that appears in not your report but in other reports." Answer: "When you have the negative of a photograph" - I'm on page now 20.354 - "you can print it in both ways.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "The Chamber is aware of that."
