And then you said: "Our intention was not by any means to change the meaning, but just to make sure that the description corresponds to the position of the vehicle. It's stated that the vehicle was in front of the evidence, and Zorka Simic was standing in front of the entrance. The projectile hit her, it exploded and caused damage, deformation, and given the position of the street where the vehicle was, this photograph corresponds to the situation." And now the final question from Judge Orie: "You turn the photograph for 180 degrees because you thought that it would fit better into what you read about the cause of events. Is that true?" Witness, answer: "Yes, that's true." So, sir, you've previously manipulated a photograph so it would fit your version of the events. Isn't that true, as you told Judge Orie?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, that's not true. It's not true because the photograph was placed at an angle of the drawing where the direction of the flight of the projectile was clearly indicated. That direction was important. And that photograph that was placed there by mistake in that way, it was a genuine error. When you look at the vehicle in that drawing, the vehicle is exactly placed where its location was, the projectile hit directly in front of that location, hit that Zorka Simic, the poor woman, and another person who died, and the conclusion of that analysis says clearly the projectile came from the west, and it is not changed in the least relative to the evidence provided earlier. It is only my mistake because I'm not a photographer that I omitted to mention that I turned that photograph and that I didn't Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond indicate that I did not use it as a basic element for my analysis. The conclusion is based on the direction of the projectile. I could even say that it is more of a manipulation to say that I manipulated the evidence. You could claim something like that if I had opposed the conclusion based on the previous evidence provided by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, when questioned by Judge Orie, you turned the photograph 180 degrees because you thought that would fit better into what you had read about the cause of the events. Is that true? And your answer is, "Yes, that's true." You didn't say "I made a mistake. I did it accidentally." You said, that's true. You intentionally turned the photograph. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That photograph was turned by mistake, and I said to Judge Orie on that occasion, and I said to everyone, that in practice nothing was changed. If I didn't change the data given me by the Prosecution, based on this or that photograph, I cannot understand how anyone can make the conclusion that that photograph was used to make an erroneous conclusion. It was clearly indicated that the projectile came from the west, just as the Prosecution material indicated. Where is the manipulation? You are now trying to challenge my expert report on this event and this hole, this crater, because you did not manage to convince me that it came from north-south. You are now trying to use this to prove that I am manipulating evidence. That is practically what you want. You want to practically discredit me as an expert witness based on your ignorance of this material.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The record speaks for itself. And you can also look at the Galic decision, and I can get the Court the footnote where they talk about the change of the photograph. Let us move on, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just before you do, Mr. Weiner, we didn't deal satisfactorily with page 40, line 12, the last word. I just note it so that it's not forgotten that the last word as shown in the transcript is "east." Mr. Petrovic says that was not the direction given by the witness in his evidence. I felt we ought to just record that so it's not lost and forgotten. We can now move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you concluded in your report, sir, that on December 6th, JNA mortar shells landed in the Old Town. Isn't that correct? Without getting into the issue of whether they were intentional or unintentional, the JNA mortar shells did in fact land within the walls of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Sorry, I must -- [Interpretation] Interpreter, you didn't interpret this properly. [In English] Mortar shells? More shells than only one shell?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, JNA mortar shells. You indicated over 100 --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because translation was only one projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is correct. I mean, in the analysis we analysed the fall of individual projectiles, shells into the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you indicated in your report that it was 82- and 120-millimetre shells fired by JNA mortars that landed in the Old Town on December 6th.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the basis of the effects of what happened at the objective and knowing what the effect of 82-millimetre and 120-millimetre mortars is, we concluded that these were 82- and 120-millimetre shells, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You indicated in your report that the shelling -- and actually today and yesterday in your testimony, that the shelling of the Old Town by the JNA came from three locations, Ledenice, Rajcevic, and Strincijera. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object to the content of the question. As this question was put, it is not contained in the evidence of this witness. Could my colleague please be very precise in terms of what was said here. [In English] Shelling of the Old Town, for example, that...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shelling of the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. We'll do it a little different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you indicated that on December 6th, JNA mortar shells fell in the Old Town as a result of mortar fire from three JNA locations, mortars at Ledenice, Rajcevic, and Strincijera. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I said, from those directions when C-3, C-4, and C-5 were fired at, individual shells did fall into the Old Town. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I didn't ask you about C-3, C-4, and C-5. I just ask you that you please just answer the questions that you're asked. Now, based on your analysis of the tapes and your analysis of the evidence and witness statements, you indicated -- or you're aware, sir, that as a result of those shells falling in the Old Town fired by JNA mortars, a great deal of damage was caused. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for the damage, there is no mention of it in the report. For five months, we listened to damage and what kind of damage this was. But that is not the subject that this report deals with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The question is going on to put this issue of damage to the witness, as I understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- proper cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you agree, sir, that as a result of JNA mortars firing shells which landed in the Old Town, a great deal of damage was caused? Do you agree with that, sir, on December 6th?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot fully agree because I did not analyse the quality, if I can put it that way, of the damage or the degree of damage. I can only say that mortar shells, that on the 6th of December, fell into the Old Town could have led to damage. What level of damage, that is something I did not analyse. But it is certain that they did lead to damage. Greater or lesser damage, depending on the projectile involved and the place where it landed. It is one thing if the projectile hit a roof, and it's a different thing if it hit a concrete slab either on a terrace or on the Stradun or a street in the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you reviewed approximately six videos, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And in each of those six videos, they depict a great deal of damage. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Damaged buildings were shown, but I keep telling you, I cannot talk to you about this because I did not analyse the level of damage. I can tell you what I observed visually. I observed buildings that were damaged or in flames; the hotel was called the Royal or the Imperial, I can't remember exactly. What I paid attention to more was the smoke because on the basis of smoke one can locate where the shell fell, or if it fell at all. And I was watching this in order to see how many projectiles could have fallen on the Old Town. And if you look at our expert report and if you look at the section that has to do with the analysis of hits in the Old Town, it says --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, sir, you're not answering the question, sir. By the way, in your report, you include the maps from the Croatian analysis of the damage, and you discuss that, too, in your report on or about pages 94, and you have the maps on 94A and B in your report. Isn't that correct, sir? 94B, the Croatian damage report, pages 94, 95, discussion of the damage, 94A, page 94, you discuss damage, the levels of damage. You even used the Croatian analysis levels 1, 2, 3, and 4. Isn't that correct? Isn't that in your report, sir? That's in the English, pages 94 on.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the English version. And this part was taken out of my analysis. However, regardless of that, if we look at page 94, the 450 items we analysed, we analysed only 1 and 2; that is to say, those 95 approximately, 95 damages. So on page --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question is, does it --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: My question is: Is this in your report? That's all. This section taken from the Croatian analysis, damage analysis. So you have reviewed the damage to the Old Town. Isn't that correct? It's right in your report, page 94, 94A, page 94B, page 95. And then you have conclusion analysis of damage caused to features within the walls of the Old Town on page 95. So you do consider or review the damage in your report.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But from the aspect of the effect of the projectile, not the degree of damage sustained by the building itself. That is where we do not understand each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm just asking you if you realise that there was a great deal of damage in the Old Town. That's all. And you do discuss it, and you show the Croatian maps indicating there was a great deal of damage. That's in your report. Isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Croatian map -- I mean, in the final version, I don't see how come you have this. In the final version of the expert opinion, we did not include this map precisely so it would not lead to this kind of confusion as we have now. Because our analysis of the damage, as I've said to you, was made from the aspect of the type of projectiles that could have fallen. And if you look at the conclusion, you can see that we say that out of a total of 27 projectiles of 120 and 79 and 82 millimetres, there could have been a certain number of damage, and then also the navy ones that are on ships in view of their trajectory, they could not target roofs in the Old Town, and they could not cause damage on roofs in the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to just check with the Court. Does the Court have these pages or is it just mine?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that is an integral part of the report as it is presented. There is no dispute about that. There is no misunderstanding. What you are showing is an integral part of the report, and the witness has it in front of him, the expert witness has it in front of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, having reviewed the videos, having looked at the analysis done by the Croatian architects, having reviewed the UN expert commission report, you're aware that as a result of the shelling on December 6th by the JNA, that some buildings were damaged. You're aware of that, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware of the fact that some buildings were damaged, but I do not agree with you. Our conclusion is not that the JNA shelled, because shelling is one thing, and the individual fall of certain projectiles as an effect of everything that I presented in the expert opinion is another thing. So you cannot conclude what I did not conclude.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We're using different terms. As a result of shells from JNA mortars falling in the Old Town, buildings were damaged. Isn't that correct? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. And I fully agree with that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And further, as a result of those shells from JNA mortars on December 6th, roofs were damaged, either holes in a roof or a whole roof just collapsed. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the pictures I did not see that an entire roof had fallen, but I did see some damage, circle-shaped, that are the effect of the fall of a mortar shell. It looks like that. Not in any picture did I see a complete roof that had fallen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Because in your report on page 90 in the English, you state, under tape number 3, "What is characteristic is the large-scale caving in of roofs on old buildings because of the action of mortar shells." That's under tape 3, the first, second, third -- fourth full paragraph. So you said: "Large-scale caving in of roofs on old buildings." So is that what you saw, large-scale caving in of roofs on old buildings?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please tell me where this is in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sure. Sir, on page 90, there is tape 2, and then there's tape 3, which is number 0062, and then it's the first paragraph, and then the second paragraph begins: "The recordings relate to damage..." The third paragraph begins: "Damage caused by mortar shells to the pavement in the Stradun..." And then the fourth full paragraph says: "What is characteristic is the large-scale caving of roofs on old buildings because of the action of mortar shells." So you saw large-scale caving in of roofs. Correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, correct. As a result of the fact that on the old roof, due to what the projectile did, there was this caving in because the beams were rotten. As far as I know, before these events, a list of buildings was compiled, buildings that had roofs that were dilapidated and very old and that could have collapsed anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you're also aware that as a result of shells falling into the Old Town fired by JNA mortars you indicated that religious buildings, you're aware that religious buildings were damaged. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But since you insist on damage, even Grbic stated before this Court in contrast to what was said here that the Orthodox church was damaged very little. On the basis of this information that we're discussing here, according to the list of damage, it seems that the Orthodox church had sustained all four levels of damage. Mr. Grbic, who knows Dubrovnik very well and who lives there, stated before this Honourable Trial Chamber that the Orthodox church had sustained very little damage. To tell you the truth, from that moment, we did not even look at this from the point of view of the level or degree of damage. We gave a description, if I can put it that way, of how the projectile could have done whatever was done, everything that I've mentioned several times, 120-millimetre, 79-, 82-millimetre shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your answer was yes, you were aware that or you had seen on the video religious buildings were damaged. And you also have to be aware that cultural buildings --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And are you aware that from listening in on some of the evidence that local residents, civilians, were injured --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really think that this line of cross-examination goes completely beyond the content of this expert report. The man was not in Dubrovnik, and he doesn't know anything about this. He is an expert in ballistics. He's an artillery man. That's what we're talking about, not about cultural monuments, not about civilians. That is outside his evidence. And also, he does not have any experience with Dubrovnik on the 6th of December 1991. I kindly ask my colleague to put questions in relation to the subject of the analysis, and that is sublimed in the conclusion of the analysis. So religious buildings, cultural monuments are things that the Honourable Trial Chamber has sufficient evidence about, and they can certainly draw conclusions on that basis. This has nothing to do with the very essence of this expert analysis. So could my learned friend please focus on what the essence of the matter is. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is very relevant evidence. This witness has indicated that other than one shell, which we're disputing, it was the JNA whose shells landed in the Old Town. And I want to just go through the damage that they caused because what he further states in his document is that the damage is consistent with the mortar shelling. He states that in one of his conclusions, that the damage is consistent. So I want to get into the extent of the damage. So because of his statements -- conclusions, this is relevant testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, I'm afraid you've lost me in your relevance. The man who is a witness here is giving evidence as a ballistics expert as to the types of weapons that he indicates were being used, as to where the fall of shells might be, et cetera. Now, we have from that got to the point that by one means or another he accepts that a large number of shells fell in the Old Town. Now, what is the point with this witness's expertise of learning that in the Old Town, among the damaged targets, were a range of different types of buildings and that as a consequence of shells falling in the occupied town people were killed or injured?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Because he claims in his conclusions that his number, which he arrives at or his estimate, it's not a specific number, it's an estimate, that the damage in the Old Town that occurred according to the Croatian study is consistent with his estimate as to the number of JNA shells that landed in the Old Town. Since he is claiming as a result that that estimate in that Croatian report is consistent with his estimate, it's consistent, therefore, I just want to go over the extent of the damage because he's saying it's consistent with his estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But what is the point that you're going to? Are you trying to say that his estimate is wrong? Or are you accepting his estimate?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, I'm not accepting his estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: How, then, is this cross-examination pursuing that line?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I just want to see if he's aware of the extent of the damage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're not dealing with extent, you're dealing with types. You're going to injuries to people, these types of monuments, buildings, et cetera. Isn't this just merely a general canvassing of the nature of the town?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, because we as Prosecution have the burden of proving that that damage was, in fact, caused by the JNA shelling, and this witness seems to be indicating in his report, he's indicating that it was. And I just want to further establish that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's the whole point. Why, then, are you going over the details again?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We accept that you have reached that point with this witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. I'll move on. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let's move to a little bit of a different area, sir. In your report on page 20 of the English, you indicate that the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade directed its fire at the Lapad area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown map 132, P132.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, what was the page reference you made? On page 20, there's no mention of it.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] 20? On page 20, in my --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, page 20, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Weiner, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If you go to the second-full paragraph, sir. One moment. Right in the middle. "The 82-millimetre and 120-millimetre mortars of the 5th Mechanised Infantry Brigade, 3rd Battalion, given the disposition of the 82 mortar firing positions in the Pobrezje sector and the 120 mortar firing positions in the Greblje sector, given their maximum ranges were unable to fire on the Dubrovnik Old Town. Their fire was directed on the firing positions of DOS forces deployed in Lapad to the west of the Old Town." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, and that's logical. In other words, what were we trying to say? 120-millimetre mortars in the region of Greblje and in the region of Pobrezje were at a location which is bigger than the maximum range of a mortar, and these mortars could not have hit the Old Town of Dubrovnik. Mortars at Greblje were over 6 and a half kilometres away, whereas 6.500 metres is the maximum range of a mortar. So they were over 6 and a half kilometres away from the Old Town. We said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I know that, the questions I have -- and you can sit down, Madam usher if you like. The question I have is are you familiar with some other locations outside the Old Town? Do you know where Babin Kuk is on the map? Are you familiar with Babin Kuk? Could you show us where Babin Kuk is.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This map, well, this is Babin Kuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, right there.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you know where Lapad is right below Babin Kuk?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is Lapad, this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you know towards the bottom corner where that dot is, the elbow of it, where the Hotel Libertas is? Are you familiar with the Hotel Libertas to the right side where the dot is?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the location precisely. This is a large-scale map, 1 to 100.000, I think. So it can barely be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown map P11, too, please, so he can see where Hotel Libertas is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is the map that Negodic -- I'm sorry, Nojko Marinovic used. And this served as a basis for us for determining the locations of the Croatian firing positions. And in the annex we have listed three, and we included this map as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking about Nojko Marinovic --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Libertas is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you see where --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Libertas is here in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you show us where it is on map 132. Could that one be taken away, please. We don't need that any more.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I just have a look. Listen, you're asking me to use a map. So quite clearly here in this bay, I think it's called Dance, this is where Libertas is, this dark dot. I don't know if you can see it clearly on your screen. That's the Libertas Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The dark dot. Now, sir --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, let me show you precisely. This is where Libertas is. Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Now, sir, there has been testimony in this case that this map is 1 to 50.000. We measured it this morning, and it came out to 1 to 71.000. I'd rather go with the larger number, which would mean that 1 millimetre is 71 metres, a centimetre is 710. Do you have a ruler with you, sir, with millimetres and centimetres? Do you have a ruler with you? Could you please measure from the 3rd of the 5th -- the mortar battalion from the 3 of the 5th first to the Babin Kuk area and tell us what the distance is. I have a ruler if you need one, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you allow me, we have a problem with this map. This map is a photocopy, of course, and we lost its scale in photocopy. So we need to know the exact scale in order for us to be able to do any measurements whatsoever. And we don't know what the scale vis-a-vis the original is on this copy. So any kind of measurement or calculation would be inappropriate if we are to do it on the basis of this map. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this map has been used throughout trial to determine distances. It has been used as 1 to 50.000. We measured it today because it is copied, and we came out to 1 to 71.000 which is more in favour of the Defence, and I'd rather use the 1 to 71.000 which is 1 millimetre is 71 metres; a centimetre is 710 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: How did you measure it today to get 1 to 71.000?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We had the military analysts unit upstairs measure it. They compared it from one map to another.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's not evidence that's going to assist us with the scale. The point made by Mr. Petrovic seems very well made. Because of photocopying, this is not a reliable scale of map.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it has been used throughout this trial. This is not the first time it has been used --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I know. All you're doing is demonstrating that the measurements made have been unreliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can the witness use the ruler and determine his own scale?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: How does he determine the scale unless he knows precisely the distance between two points on the map of his own knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's what they basically did in the map unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's not this witness. We haven't heard the map unit give evidence. Mr. Petrovic, it seems to be accepted that in the photocopying, the scale is not produced faithfully. It is from a series as I understand it of 1 to 50.000, but it is no longer to that scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we use P10 which is a map to scale. If he could compare the two maps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If he can do that, he can tell us approximately the scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Or do you have one of your maps with a scale with you? Because I noticed on your maps, the two maps you photocopied in your report, you both had scales, I think one was 1 to 50.000 and the other was 1 to 25.000. Do you have those with you today, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's possible. I have already established this. And I can say that the fire position of the firing group of the 5th Battalion -- I'm sorry, of the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Motorised Infantry Brigade is at 7.800 metres from the Old Town as the crow flies. In other words, these mortars were not able to target the Old Town because the maximum range is 6.423 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. My question was what is the distance to Babin Kuk, if you can determine that, from those mortars, the 3rd of the 5th to Babin Kuk, sir? If you could please do that.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly speaking, 5.000 metres given the fact that this is a large map. So practically 5.000 metres, which is more than two-thirds of the maximum range of a mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. So if you look at Babin Kuk, it's part of a peninsula, a roundish or an oval, horizontal peninsula. Is that whole area of Babin Kuk within the range of those 120-millimetre mortars?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's at the very far end of the range. But not the whole area; the ultimate point of the peninsula, and if your scale is correct, I haven't checked it, so 78 --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that would --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that the scale of this map is 1 to 60.000. The ultimate range is -- well, there's no chance that this ultimate point -- if you ask me about the lower edge at the seashore and if you would ask me to hit the shore of this peninsula, I'm talking about the point located horizontally between point 6 and point 8, and the point --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Can we continue this cross-examination if we have proper map in front of the witness with full and proper scale, no photocopies and precise scale. Any conclusion can only be based on this kind of material, so I kindly ask Your Honour to instruct that this cross-examination continue based on the proper map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an original map, 1 to 25.000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Mr. Petrovic. We understand from the witness that he is aware of the scale difference and of the general distances in the area. And he has both a proper-scale map and the distorted one. And on those bases, I think this cross-examination is proceeding on, and the witness is providing reliable distances. He's doing the double measurement, as it were. That's from what I can see. And I would take it from the head nodding of the witness that is correct as well. So I appreciate your concern, but I think the witness is aware of the problem and is correcting it as he goes. Thank you, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So the island of Babin Kuk is within the range of the 120-millimetre mortars at the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 4.250 metres is to the centre of the peninsula. That is what I conclude as I watch as this 1 to 25.000 scale map, 120-millimetre mortar position, and if we view the very top point of Babin Kuk lies at 3 -- 4.300 metres, or rather, 4.250 metres, I don't know which exactly point you want me to discuss. Now, you asked me about Libertas, and if you want to know this range --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the distance to Libertas is 6.250 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Therefore, sir, since a mortar, a 120-millimetre mortar has a range of 6340 metres, approximately 6340, the Libertas Hotel is within the range of the 120-millimetre mortars on -- of the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade? Just within the range.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be precise, it is at 6.125 metres. That is at the farthest end of the range, that is about 200 metres to the full range, or let's say 150 metres. So the Libertas is at 6.150. But you know, using an ultimate range limit and to target an objective there is not very feasible and practicable because it depends on various other elements like weather conditions and position of firing. In principle, mortars are never used to target the objectives which are beyond two-thirds of their maximum range. They may hit or maybe fire randomly, but they can hardly hit the target. As I said, 7.000 metres was the distance between the Old Town of Dubrovnik and the Greblje where the 120-millimetre mortars were. Therefore, they were incapable of hitting the Old Town from that distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But all I'm saying is the mortars of the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade, if we look at those mortars, the Libertas Hotel area is within the range. It's at the outer limits, but it's still 150 to 200 metres within the range. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they're at the very far end of the range.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll probably start a new area, and it...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Weiner. I think that's probably a convenient time to break. And we'll resume at 2.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.57 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Your Honour, I have two items for the Court. I have the judgement and opinion of Stanislav Galic, and I invite the Court's attention to paragraph 393 and footnote 1338. I have copies for the Court and all parties. That's what I referred to earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Weiner, do you have some questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: One more thing, Your Honour. I read from a transcript from Galic, I said pages 20.364 and 20.365.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Apparently, the copying machine copied multiple pages of 20.364. I'll get that at the next break, Your Honour. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Good afternoon, Mr. Vilicic.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you testified yesterday and today about the meteorological effects of shells. Do you recall that? That's also listed in your report.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you testified that the problem was or the major problem was this wind which you called Bura.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that's a wind that moves north to south?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The main direction of the Bura wind is northeast.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. So it runs from northeast to southwest?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Normally. Relative to the position of Dubrovnik, it blows from land to sea. And all the projectiles that are fired are pushed towards Dubrovnik. In fact, all the trajectories are deflected from positions VP-3 and VP-4.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, there's another wind that also is involved or is also seen in the area of Dubrovnik, and that's called a Jugo, did I pronounce it correctly? Something like that, Jugo?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that moves from south to north from the sea to the land?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main direction of the Jugo wind is south-north, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. With the Court's permission, can Exhibit P19 be shown from 10 minutes to 10 minutes and 38 seconds, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you stop right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise that area? Do you know where that is? Do you recognise the Old Town harbour?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you let that continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You'll notice, sir, the smoke is blowing north, maybe slightly northwest. Isn't that a Jugo wind?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And do you see the date on that video?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's December 6th, 1991?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So there were times when there was not a Bura wind, but there was a Jugo wind blowing away from the city.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the Bura wind to transform into a Jugo, that has not happened yet. Obviously what happens here is a quite different effect. Above Dubrovnik, there occurs a circulation of a strong Bura wind blowing from land to sea creating a vacuum on the slope below Srdj, and there occurs a circular movement of area. Why don't you take the Djelo Jusic film which served as a basis, apart from witness testimony, for claiming that the Bura was so strong that branches of trees swayed, swaying as we can see in the film towards land, not towards the sea.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you just saw on the video that there was a Uga wind as opposed to a Bura. And if there is a Jugo wind, it is blowing away from the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The witness said in the previous answer that the branches swayed towards the sea.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Jugo doesn't have to blow here. This can happen even before the wind. We're talking here about two argus vessels which were not hit, two argus vessels in the old harbour which were not hit on the 6th of December. Therefore, this figure on the 6th of December does not correspond to the setting on fire of these two ships which were anchored in the old harbour of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you based certain conclusions on the fact that there was a Bura wind affecting the shells. If there was not a Bura wind, but in fact Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond it was a Jugo wind blowing north, blowing away from the Old Town, wouldn't that affect your conclusions?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not change the main conclusion because if you remember in the depiction of results, we primarily analysed and showed here the analysis discounting the impact of the lateral wind. And all the testimony we had here, primarily that of Djelo Jusic who was there said that there was an extremely strong Bura wind blowing. Djelo Jusic said everybody knows about the Dubrovnik Bura. There is no reason to doubt that Djelo Jusic who is a local and who is making that film that day is wrong. And the film shows clearly that the branches were swaying from land towards the sea. And I am not familiar with any case, although I was frequently on the coast and I have a house there, where the Bura wind would turn into the Jugo. Jugo is characterised by low pressure, whereas the Bura wind is characterised by high pressure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I never said that a Bura would transfer into a Jugo. However, sir, since there is a Jugo wind as you admit, you're looking at a Jugo wind blowing away. My question is does that affect your dispersion calculations? Because you're basing those on the basis of a Bura wind, if there was not a Bura wind, that would change your calculations or your statistics would be changed.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it would not. All that would happen, that data involving the Bura wind would be excluded. But I cannot understand that the Bura wind was actually blowing, and you are showing me a picture involving a Jugo. In the course of one day, there cannot be such a sharp change in pressure wherein the Bura would transform or change into a Jugo. Jugo is a characteristic of a field of low pressure, whereas a Bura wind is characteristic of a field of high pressure. I can also remind you of the general report for ten years of the institute for meteorology.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, on page 88 of your conclusions, you say "bad meteorological conditions and an extremely strong wind - Bura - on 6 December 1991, in particular, considerably contributed to the diversion of trajectory of projectiles fired from all positions, VP-1, VP-3, and VP-4, towards the Dubrovnik Old Town which also resulted in a higher number of projectiles landing within the walls of the Dubrovnik Old Town." Now, if there was not an extremely strong Bura wind but a Jugo wind, would not that affect your dispersion statistics? Because apparently from this conclusion, you based them on a strong Bura wind.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only on that, please. I have stated clearly that the basic analysis shown here speaks of dispersion after abbreviated and simple preparation and correction of firing without the influence of wind. And then in the next step in every case, such as 4.3, if you remember, is without the impact of wind, when you fire from VP-1 at C-3, involving impact of wind. It is clear that the impact of wind only increases the probability of shells landing within the Old Town. And I have additional data to prove it if you need.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that's what you say on page 50. "As a result of the effect of the gale blowing from the land towards the sea during the flight of projectiles, their trajectories deviated in terms of deflection. Since the firing positions of the JNA mortars were positioned laterally in relation to the selected targets, the effect of the wind naturally led to the deviation of projectiles towards the sea, toward the old -- i.e., towards the Dubrovnik Old Town." Sir, if the wind was blowing the other way, would not that same strong wind blow the shells or projectiles away from the Old Town of Dubrovnik? If it's blowing from north to south, you claim it blows them in. So if it's blowing from south to north, that should blow them away. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. That is correct. However, you are overlooking one thing: Namely, the intensity of the Jugo wind is much lower than that of the Bura wind.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let us move on. In your report, sir, you estimate the number of JNA mortar shells that fell within the Old Town walls. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could fall within the Old Town, not that fell, but that could have landed within the Old Town. That is a big difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And your estimate, sir, is based on the number of mortars at each of the three locations and the number of combat sets that each of those mortars fired. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conclusion was based on the assumption of 100 fired shells or projectiles and on the assumption of one fired combat kit, that is, that each mortar fired one combat kit that, namely, 160 shells were fired from VP-1, 240 from Rajcevic, and another number from Strincijera. That is 360. 360, yes, from Strincijera.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you based that, sir, according to the footnote - we're on page 89, that's conclusion number 9, and it refers to footnote number 68 - and in footnote --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt my learned friend. A part of the witness's answer did not enter the record on page 72 from lines 13 to 18. I would not like to interpret now what was actually said in order not to lead the witness, but I would just like to point out that the answer on record is not the complete answer the witness provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. Mr. Weiner, would you follow that up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sure, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I asked you earlier, in your report, you estimate the number of JNA mortar shells that fell within the Old Town walls. You made an estimate. I'm adding that. You made an estimate. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could have landed in the Old Town under the circumstances I described if one combat kit had been fired per mortar. [In English] I use conditional, and you are always using present.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Correct, sir. Now, you based this estimate as to one combat kit fired per mortar, and this is on page 89 of your report, footnote 68, on the 9th VPS war diary and a statement from Zlatan Jeremic. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, first, would you agree that in the war diary, there are no reports as to the number of shells fired from any of those three locations. There is a report as to the number of shells fired on one occasion from the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade, but there is no indication as to the number of shells at any of those three JNA locations. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that the diary only notes the firing of the mortar from the Greblje location of the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade. However, in the war diary in an earlier entry I found the quantities of ammunition requested for those mortars. I don't know the page number exactly, but I know it says that in total, about 200 shells were required for the 120-millimetre mortar and that in another request, 200 shells were requested for 82-millimetre mortars. I spoke to the commander of that combat group of 120-millimetre mortars, Jankovic [as interpreted], and he told me that on that day, he fired 17 smoke shells --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: First, who did you speak to and --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jeremic, Zlatan --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Because I noticed you did refer to Zlatan Jeremic. Are you aware that Zlatan Jeremic was not a witness in this case? Are you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was not. But I also know very well, I received information, that he was the commander of the combat mortar group of 120-millimetre mortars from Ledenice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, he was not a witness in this case, and none of his statements have been introduced into this case. Are you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware of that. But I'm not aware of the fact that if certain information becomes available to me, I'm not allowed to present it to this Court. Nobody told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, are you aware, sir, that the information from Zlatan Jeremic, whatever information you have, as well as that earlier -- that earlier request in the diary are not in evidence in this case? Are you aware of that? Or am I just telling you this for the first time?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Zlatan Jeremic was not a witness in this trial. At the moment when I talked to Zlatan Jeremic, he was not a witness as far as I know. He had not appeared before this Honourable Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And no statements from Mr. Jeremic, whether oral or written, have been introduced into this Court. Are you aware of that, at this trial? No statements of Mr. Zlatan Jeremic have been introduced, isn't that correct, since you have been --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know when I talked to Mr. Zlatan Jeremic, my first question to him was whether he had been engaged by the Tribunal, whether he was supposed to be a witness there. And then he said to me no. And then it was only logical that I said to him, then, "Okay, tell me please where was the location?" That was the primary thing that interested me. Where the 120-millimetre mortar was located precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that information that you received as to the location, his statement as to location, is also not evidence in this case. Are you aware of that now? Would you accept my statement that his -- Zlatan Jeremic's statement as to the location, as to the amount of shells that he fired are not evidence in this case? On December 6th -- I'm sorry, you're nodding your head in the up and down direction.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I nodded. I don't agree. I do not agree with you in order to establish the truth, we cannot mention the exact location in our expert report. Please, on the basis of which report submitted for the expert analysis can there be a different location?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question to you is are you aware that his statement as to the location or any statement from Zlatan Jeremic is not in evidence in this Court? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I'm an engineer. I do not know the legal regulations sufficiently in order to be giving the right answers to such questions. You are putting legal questions to me, and I'm not qualified to answer them. I'm not a legal expert. I am answering technical questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking you if you're a legal expert. You testified this morning that you had monitored the trial, either today or yesterday, that you have been monitoring the trial over the Internet. Are you aware that Zlatan Jeremic has not been a witness in this case? That's all. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have said so already, that I did know that he was not a witness here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, you weren't in any of those three JNA mortar positions on December 6th, 1991. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, I'm -- I was a member of the military technical institute on that day, and there is no logic in my being at any one of those positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So that's a no? I take that as a no, you were not at any of those positions.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is only logical that I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In fact, you weren't anywhere in the Dubrovnik area on December 6th, 1991. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And from where you were, you could not witness any of the mortar firing from any of those three JNA positions. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not have been the witness, and I do not understand how come an expert who does an analysis for a particular matter has to be on the spot in order to give answers. I find your question to be totally illogical. You're asking an expert to confirm that he was not at a firing position, and I am doing an expert opinion ten years after all this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, just --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More than ten years.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you some simple questions. Would you just please answer them. Now, according to your report, you do not possess any records, JNA records, as to the number of shells fired from each of those mortars on the 6th of December 1991. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. That's correct. And the entire expert opinion is based on 100 projectiles and one combat kit. And another thing that is mentioned in the expertise: According to norms for destroying a particular target, how many projectiles should be fired in order to destroy a particular target. We do not use any other information.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Correct. So basically, sir, you're basing your estimate on an assumption as to the number of sets used, you're assuming the amount of ammunition that they could have had. It's all a group of assumptions, and from that you're making an estimate.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let's take it slowly, then. Sir, you weren't present. And not being present, you cannot state or you did not witness the exact number of shells fired from each mortar. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you have never seen any written records indicating the number of shells fired from each mortar, each JNA mortar at those three locations. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, too, that I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you can only estimate the number of shells fired from each of those three locations.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, I'm not estimating anything. The expertise does not give any estimate. The expertise says specifically that if 100 shells were fired on certain conditions, the result will be such and such. If one combat kit is fired, that is to say, of a group of mortars, then there can be a certain number of hits. Nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you begin each of those statements "if 100 shells are fired," "if a certain number of kits are fired." You can only estimate the number of shells fired or the number of kits fired because you weren't there to obtain the exact number. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you a direct answer. It is true that I was not there. But I cannot understand that you keep on insisting on this estimate, how many hits there would be in the case of 100 projectiles or one combat kit, and you want to generalise that for an overall situation. That was not the aim of my analysis. I did not have the right elements for firing data for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm not interested right now as to the number of impacts. I'm interested as the number of shells fired. That's why I'm saying since you weren't there to count at each of those mortars the numbers fired, there are no records as to the numbers fired, you have to begin each of your statements with "if 100 was fired," "if 1 or 2 kits were fired." You cannot give us an exact number of shells fired on that day. Isn't that correct, you can't state that?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, that I cannot say how many because I do not have any such records.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with your dispersion examples that we had throughout your report, you would vary the number of shells that could have fallen within the Old Town based on the type of preparation, whether full preparation was used, simple preparation, abbreviated preparation. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And if we use either simple, abbreviated, or even full preparation, you can't state for certain how many shells were fired at a target as part of the initial preparation before it hit the target, before we have the corrections and the full firing.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You can only estimate. You can say maybe ten were fired, maybe six were fired, maybe three were fired. All you can do is estimate that. Isn't that correct? An almost-guess.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you: Each case is specific. The infantry rules for 82-millimetre mortars spell this out exactly. That is, the methodology of how primary or preliminary targeting is carried out in order to have the corrections carried out eventually. If I have time, then I could correct with one weapon. If as the situation was on the 6th of December that all of a sudden fire has to be opened at a -- in a completely different direction, in completely new firing positions then it is quite clear that a correction cannot be made with one weapon only and then to wait for the calculations for all. In that case, there is a so-called burst of fire, the entire battery fires one after the other. And then on the basis of the assessment of the fall of the shell, but the minimum is three groups of shells. It even has to be verified, the angle of firing, even five groups fire. So it is correct that I do not know how many groups were fired, but the minimum had to be three projectiles if he had time to use one weapon only, or a minimum of 12 projectiles if in view of the situation he had to use four -- or rather to convey fire quickly, to move fire quickly to other targets. So it's very hard to assess this, especially in view of the situation, especially if he had to look for the target. If he did not observe the target correctly, then perhaps he even had to fire several groups under such conditions before he realised what the exact situation was that he was close to the desired target; that is to say, that projectiles were falling close to the desired target.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And since you were not there and we have no records, you can't tell if it was three that were fired as part of the initial preparation or if it was 12 that were fired or if they all had to fire without the full corrections. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Because you also know that it's possible even with the simplest preparations, simple preparations, that you could initially fire towards a target and hit it on the initial -- on the initial shot? It's possible?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this is in theory. In theory, yes. Practically, very rarely. Especially in these conditions. Again, I refer to the weather situation. It doesn't have to be the wind only. The fact is that firing positions are at an altitude which is high above the targets. They do not have the meteorological situation, air pressure, the temperature, the exact temperature of the gunpowder charges. Then also the regimen of each and every individual weapon. In such a situation, there is no chance. That would be pure lottery to hit the target with the first shell. That has never happened in my career even after 100.000 firings that we hit the target immediately unless certain ranges were studied beforehand and we had all the necessary elements.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to speak slower.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you worked as a research scientist. You weren't a soldier in a mortar battery. Now, if you do hit it on the first shot, then the other mortars would all have the corrected data after that. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And there would be less dispersion.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move a little bit on from that, sir. You're familiar with the area north of the Old Town known as Bosanka? If you're not, you could take your map out or we could use one of our maps, map 132.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could use a map. I am familiar with Bosanka, but right this minute I could not place it if I didn't have a map available.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's between Zarkovica and Srdj.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, I cannot give you answers on the basis of this map. It is such a large-scale map that I cannot recognise locations exactly. Please, then it's better to look at my map, the 1 to 25.000 one, and then I can tell you exactly what is because this one is one that I'm not familiar with and also the scale is very big. Also, the markings can barely be seen. Well, fortunately I can see Bosanka here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Doctor, please, look at your own map for a moment and familiarise yourself with Bosanka.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw Bosanka even on this map. Yes, I've seen Bosanka. Yes. Should I put it here on the overhead projector?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. This is Bosanka. This is the settlement of Bosanka.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you see it looks like it's approximately 2 kilometres from the Old Town of Dubrovnik? Approximately?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, if you need accurate information... Well, let's say that was it, but it's less, I think. Less. Zarkovica -- I know Zarkovica. Zarkovica is about 2.300 metres. Bosanka, of course, is closer. Now, it's hard to see...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What is closer to the Old Town, Strincijera or Bosanka? Isn't Bosanka slightly closer?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bosanka is closer to the Old Town. Strincijera is further away, much further away.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, in your report you indicated --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: -- on page 2 --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: -- that you - you can sit down, Mr. Usher - you indicated on page 2 that you had considered the witness testimony of Admiral Jokic as part of your report. You state that on page 2 with your list. It's number 7 on your list of items that you reviewed. And did you, in fact --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, item 7. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you, in fact, consider the testimony of Admiral Jokic? Did you in fact do that?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His oral statement, yes. If he drew any maps, I wasn't able to see that. Since you provided on the Internet only partial broadcast. In fact, there's only audio broadcast. There's no video on the internet. So I did read the transcripts. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, having reviewed Admiral Jokic's testimony, you should be aware that he testified that there were four mortars with the JNA unit at Bosanka. That's on page 4.014 and 4.015, March 26th. Could you please show us in your report you refer to four mortars, those 82-millimetre mortars, located on Bosanka? Where in your report do you refer to those four mortars?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made no reference to them because practically they were not relevant for this analysis of ours. I personally believe that this information is incorrect. Admiral Jokic is not very knowledgeable about the locations where the JNA weapons were positioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you are -- are you trying to tell us that you were in a better position to know where the JNA weapons were on December 6th, 1991, than Admiral Jokic, who was the commander of the 9th VPS, that you knew better than he did where his units were? Is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, where in your report do you have the dispersion statistics or the dispersion graphs in relation to the firing of those four mortars at any of those alleged targets outside the Old Town? Where -- any firing from Bosanka at those three alleged or four alleged targets outside the Old Town, where in your report do you have that? Do you have any calculations relating to shell dispersion from mortars firing from Bosanka?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Bosanka is not covered by the expert analysis, but if it is necessary I can do it at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now if those four mortars on Bosanka fired at those targets you alleged in your report which were just outside the walls of the Old Town, would not some of those shells have dispersed into the Old Town, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was possible. But depending on the targets that they were engaging.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. So it's possible some of those shells could have been dispersed and that would increase your numbers as to the number of shells that fell within the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you want me to tell you precisely, let us take the primary direction. If target C-4 was fired at from Bosanka and if shells missed the target, then they would have fallen into the southern part of the Old Town, all of them, given the azimuth of direction of firing at C-4 from Bosanka. Had they been firing at C-5 and C-3, the same situation would occur as happened with the mortars fired from Dubac and Rajcevic. We would have had the same situation in regard to the wind effects.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. So as a result, if you did consider Bosanka, you would have found that additional shells fell within the Old Town. Yes or no? If we add Bosanka to the list of mortars firing.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't agree exactly with you. If I took into consideration ten mortar batteries, that would increase the number of shells ten times. But since I focussed my entire analysis on the assumption that had this been fired, the result would have been that. So that would apply to Bosanka as it did on Strincijera and other positions. We have established that I could not find out how many shells were fired. There were no records. And therefore, we cannot say what you just said, that more shells would have fallen. Had I had accurate data about the shells fired, I would have been in a position to say, yes, either more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, if we use the same statistics or calculations that you've used for the other sets of mortars or the other mortar batteries, that each mortar fired approximately one set of shells, so if each of those 82-millimetre mortars fired approximately one set of shells, would not that increase the number of shells that would fall within the walls of the Old Town as a result of dispersion?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the report that you have in front of you had been compiled for one year in a very accurate and meticulous manner, and it contains all the details necessary to draw the conclusions that this report contains. My learned colleague is now expecting the expert witness within a couple of seconds give his judgement on something that he had been working in similar situations for months. This is quite simply not a serious approach, and I don't think it is fair to expect this kind of view and judgement whereas for the same judgement in a different situation, months were required to achieve that. Therefore, I believe that further insistence along this line of questioning is improper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I can't agree, Mr. Petrovic. I think the propositions being put are rather straightforward, logical matters, not matters of complexity, and the witness ought to be able to deal with those. Carry on, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you like me to ask the question again?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If we use the same calculations and statistics that you used for each of the other mortar batteries, that each of the mortars in each battery fired one set of mortar shells, those were your estimates, if we use those same estimates for the mortars on Bosanka that each of the four fired one set of shells, would not that -- would not additional shells have fallen within the walls of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can give you an explicit answer based on high level of probability, and that is that C-4 was not fired at from Bosanka. I based that on the fact that the appropriate number of shells did not land in the southern part of the Old Town. If we base our assumptions on 100 shells, as an ad hoc conclusion I can tell you that Bosanka did not fire at C-4. As for the remaining elements, I'm afraid I wouldn't be able to give you a precise answer because I would need to make a rough estimate of the charge, of the distances of C-3 and C-5 targets, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your answer sounds very much like Mr. Petrovic's objection, sir. All I'm asking you for is the following: Doesn't common sense tell you that additional shells would have fallen? I'm not asking for an exact number. I don't want any precise number. But doesn't common sense tell you if you fire a hundred shells in the vicinity of the Old Town, some are going to disperse into the Old Town? Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not, no. You obviously tend to overlook one fact. We are talking about much shorter ranges, which consequently affects the pattern of dispersion, which is considerably decreased than in the cases that we had under consideration. So I cannot say that as in the cases I have analysed it would have reached the Old Town. My rough estimate is that the range was between 1.000 or 1.200 metres; the farthest one would be C-3 at 1.300 metres. At 1.000 metres, probably the dispersion elements are much lower than if we take into consideration 3.000-metre range from Rajcevic or from Strincijera, which is much farther away, almost twice or two and a half times farther from the town. I don't know where exactly on Bosanka the mortars were positioned, so I cannot apply any logic and claim that they would have fallen in -- inside the Old Town. My impression is that they wouldn't because all those previous cases never covered the entire area of the Old Town by firing from 3.500 metres. Apparently, they would never reached the Old Town, but without proper calculations I cannot give you an ad hoc answer. I would need to have firing tables in front of me. I can say that at a thousand metres, the VD value is about 8 to 10 metres. That is the deflection. And if a target is at 200 metres away, there is no chance that those shells would have fallen inside the Old Town. That applies both to C-4 and C-5. We already said that this particularly applied to C-3 in Bogosica Park that were outside the range of 82-millimetre mortars that, as you say, were at Bosanka. And these shells also would not have reached the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But, sir, in your own words, you can only offer your impression because you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, in your own words you can only offer your impression because you haven't done those calculations. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But I can make an estimate based on my expertise and knowledge on mortar dispersion values.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's interesting because you had previously indicated that you couldn't make any -- offer any expert opinion, that you need time. Let's move on, sir. There were also recoilless weapons on top of Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. There is information that there were recoilless guns at Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And those recoilless guns were overlooking the Old Town of Dubrovnik, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And are you aware of the range of those recoilless guns? We were told that they were 82-millimetre recoilless guns -- 82-millimetre weapons, guns, on top of Zarkovica. Are you aware of the range?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I was one of the designers of that gun, and I was awarded an army prize for this gun. So I know fully well about this gun. It is intended for targets up to 60 -- 600 metres, exceptionally up to 1.000 metres. And we have provided a table for --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will the witness please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For any range beyond 1.000 metres, the recoilless gun does not have a sight that can use it. They can only use the firing tables and quadrants and try to reach the targets beyond their operational range, and these are recoilless, anti-armour weapons with cumulative shells intended to pierce armour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nesic testified that there were 82-millimetre guns on top of Zarkovica. What is the range of those 82-millimetre guns that were on top of Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The effective range of reactive M72 shell is 1.000 metres. It has been designed to shoot up to 1.000 metres. The standard B82, M60 shell is intended for targets at up to 600 metres. Anything beyond those ranges is not something to be fired at with the recoilless gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I believe Mr. Nesic testified yesterday that he fired both Maljutkas and the recoilless guns at what he believed to be targets along the walls of the Old Town on the ramparts. Could you reach the Old Town with those recoilless weapons?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
