utterances.text: The maximum range makes it possible for a projectile to reach the target, but they cannot aim through a sight. They can only make a rough estimate of the direction and to take an angle by using a quadrant.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Using your map, could you measure the distance from Zarkovica to the Old Town. Could you please do that for us.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Approximately over 2.000 metres. Let me tell you that what I would be doing now to make -- making these kind of measurements would be inaccurate. We have been using the so-called coordinate metre, which is a special instrument. We had a fully flat map without wrinkles as the one that I have in front of me, so that with coordinate metre, I can make measurements with the margin of error of 25 metres. But to give you a rough estimate, and that this would later be used against me as if I had something very explicitly --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... just try to find an approximation, so it's a little over 2.000 metres, 2200, 2300 metres from Zarkovica. So it's your opinion that the shells from the recoilless cannons -- the shells from the recoilless cannons could have hit the Old Town walls or struck areas along the ramparts of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To put it better, they could reach at a stretch up to a length of 2.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, as part of your calculations, did you determine whether any shells fired by the recoilless cannons penetrated the Old Town walls? Did you consider that as part of your report?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have said since I was one of the designers and I was a designer of the active-reactive shell for the 82-millimetre recoilless gun, I can say that the projectile for the recoilless gun of 82 millimetres can pierce a reinforced concrete wall up to 100 millimetres. A projectile from a recoilless gun, because it is activated upon impact on the wall, it disintegrates, and the cumulative jet of which I can tell you the approximate thickness because I made tests, the resulting hole is about 50 millimetres in diameter. And when it comes out, the diameter is about 10 millimetres. So there is no chance for this projectile to pierce a wall of that thickness. It disintegrates before the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: My question is did you make any determinations or write any calculations or any sections of your report relating to the possibility of shells or projectiles from recoilless cannons entering the Old Town? Is that included --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. What is included are all artillery and mortar shells in the chapter that speaks about the piercing capacity of these projectiles, plus a table is given.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And I notice in one of the videotapes that you reviewed you indicated in your report that you saw a Maljutka shell enter the Old Town and hit the wall of a building. Did you include any section in your report in relation as to the number of Maljutka shells fired into the walls or inside of the walls of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. Because a Maljutka is a guided anti-armour projectile, and what I said about the recoilless projectile is also true of the Maljutka. Upon impact on the wall, it disintegrates, and it is only the cumulative jet that can continue the piercing process. Certainly not the entire projectile. On one film, however, I saw a part of the rocket engine. It was the front wall -- no, sorry. I think it was around the fish shop on the right towards Revelin. On the wall, you can see the tail end of the rocket engine, the stabiliser without the wings. You can only see the carrier of these jet fins without the fins themselves. And it is stuck in the hole, and it is protruding from it. Only based on that we concluded that one Maljutka hit the wall. But if you're asking me for an analysis and if you're asking me whether we computed or calculated the number of projectiles fired, we did not do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That was my question, sir. Thank you. All right, let's move to another area, sir. On page 99 of your Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond report, you have "General conclusions." I'd like to read your general conclusion. "On the basis of analysing JNA force's actions at the Dubrovnik battleground, primarily on the basis of information that Prosecution Witness Nojko Marinovic and Zeljko Soldo gave to Tribunal representatives, and also in the testimony at the Tribunal by Nojko Marinovic in the case IT-02-54-T of 3 April 2003, as well as other Prosecution witnesses" - in the footnote you refer to Senior Lieutenant Zoran Primic - "it cannot be concluded that fire from JNA mortars and artillery and other naval pieces was primarily directed to Dubrovnik Old Town as its primary target." Sir, first, are you aware that Zoran Primic's statement was not admitted into evidence in this case? Are you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had that piece of information, and I had the statement available to me. I had the complete statement of Nojko Marinovic, including diagrams, the layout of the city of Dubrovnik where he in his own hand indicated the disposition of firing positions of the Croatian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm not trying to be rude, Doctor, just a simple question. Were you aware that Zoran Primic's statement was not admitted as a piece of evidence in this case? Just are you aware?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until this moment, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And are you also aware or would you accept that Zoran Primic was not a witness in this case? His testimony is not before this Tribunal. Would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I accept that. But I had in my hands an official document of the ICTY about his statement to the investigators.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you indicated that your primary sources, because you relied primarily on the basis of information of Nojko Marinovic and Zeljko Soldo, are you aware that those people that you primarily relied on were not witnesses in this case? Or will you accept from me today that these were not witnesses in this case?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, please, based on what were we supposed to make this expert report to present it to you today if not the documents we received from the Tribunal, or rather the Defence team with in its turn received it from the Tribunal. You're really asking me impossible questions. How was I supposed to make an expert report without any documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you some questions. When I finish, Defence counsel will ask you questions, and you'll be able to explain whatever you would like. But would you please answer my questions, sir. Would you accept from me, and actually having monitored this case, you've indicated you've monitored this case, you should be aware that Nojko Marinovic and Zeljko Soldo were not witnesses in this case. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I have not heard them in this case, and I was surprised, especially after the testimony of Mr. Negodic, that the commander of artillery should know better what the situation in Dubrovnik was than the commander of the city's defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And are you also aware that those statements that you read, their statements to the OTP, have not been admitted as evidence in this case? Are you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm hearing this from you for the first time. I had opportunity while monitoring this case of hearing from you, or rather the Office of the Prosecutor, that the final decision whether to forego Nojko Marinovic's testimony has not been made. So to date, I have not been informed that Nojko Marinovic's definitively ruled out from this case. Listening to you, I know that it is in the process of consideration, and I'm just trying to explain now what I'm aware of and what I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just, please, just answer my question so we can finish and we can finish today the cross-examination. Are you aware that the statements of Nojko Marinovic, Zeljko Soldo, Zoran Primic have not been introduced as evidence in this case? Are you aware of that? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was making my expert report, I was not aware that they were not introduced as witnesses because handling official documents of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Fine, no problem with that, sir. Are you aware that Nojko Marinovic's testimony in that case, the numbers you referred to, that's the Milosevic case, that Nojko Marinovic's testimony in the Milosevic case, the transcripts of that testimony have not been introduced in this case? Are you aware of that? His Milosevic testimony --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know -- or rather, it is logical that that transcript has not been introduced in this case. But the reason why we quoted that case is the fact that Nojko Marinovic fully confirmed in that other case the statement he gave in writing to this Tribunal in year 2001, and for me it was a basis for concluding that Nojko Marinovic spoke the truth on two occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question isn't your view of Nojko Marinovic's veracity. My question is are you aware that Nojko Marinovic's testimony in the Milosevic case has not been admitted in this case? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm hearing from you now, today, that you are not introducing even Nojko Marinovic in this case. And therefore, it follows logically that you are not going to introduce this second part either. I heard personally at the end of the cross-examination by the Prosecution that the final decision on whether Nojko Marinovic will be a witness or not has not been made yet. So for us who are doing the expert report, the possibility was still relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All I'm saying is you know now that Nojko Marinovic's Milosevic case testimony has not been admitted. Now, sir, you've -- now, sir, you mentioned Mr. Primic in footnote 74.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. And that you indicated on that same page, and that's part of the conclusion, you've indicated that Mr. Primic was commander of the mortars in Bogosica Park and fired 3.000 mortar shells on that date. Having read Mr. Primic's statement, does he not indicate at page 5 that he was not at Bogosica Park on that date, and why didn't you state that in your document, that Mr. Primic states that he was not at Bogosica Park on that date?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether this translation is correct. What it says here is Zoran Primic was commander of the battery of the first group of mortars located in Bogosica Park, and then there is a mistake. It says that on that day, he fired 3.000 shells. That's written in the B/C/S. However, I saw later that in the original English, it says 300 shells. Therefore, I made a correction from 3.000 to 300. The mistake I made originated from the translation error.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, you're aware that according to the testimony of -- or are you aware of the testimony in this case from Mr. Negodic as well as the statement which you relied on from Mr. Primic, he indicates that he was not at Bogosica Park at that date and that the mortars at Bogosica Park did not fire on that date. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot agree with you for the following reason: Although you do not acknowledge or recognise Nojko Marinovic at this moment, Nojko Marinovic clearly says that in Bogosica Park there were 82-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]....

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allow me to tell you --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He has not testified in this case and his evidence isn't before this Chamber. You relied on this document, sir, and in this document he states on page 5, "My two mortars that fired at Srdj were located in a small soccer field behind the SDK building. I had moved them a day or two before. My other two mortar teams in Bogosica Park did not fire that day. I remained with the two mortar teams behind the SDK building." In any of the footnotes relating to Zoran Primic, you did not state that he was not -- he did not fire from Bogosica Park and that he indicates there was no firing from Bogosica Park on that day. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, you are claiming that there was no firing position of 82-millimetre mortars in Bogosica Park ever --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, the document you relied upon is making that claim. But did you put that in any footnote? All I'm asking is did you place in a footnote that the document you are relying on states there was no firing from Bogosica Park? Then we can take a break if the Court allows us.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, here in footnote number 74, you are making a linkage between two things. In footnote 74, it says: "statement by Senior Lieutenant Zoran Primic, commander of the first group of mortars in Bogosica Park. On the 6th of December, he fired 3.000, or rather 300 on JNA positions, 300 shells." And you are now telling me that I said that he fired 300 shells, or rather 3.000 as it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question to you is, do you state in that footnote or anywhere else this person who I am relying upon has indicated that he did not fire from Bogosica Park on that date, or that mortars didn't fire from Bogosica Park on that date? Do you state that in that footnote or anywhere else where you mention Zoran Primic? That's the only question I have for you. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, I am relying on Zoran Primic that he fired 3.000 shells on that day. It was -- it's an enormous quantity, and I found it surprising. I later received information that it was only 300 shells in total and that was corroborated by Negodic as well. Why would I invoke -- I never considered or said anywhere that Zoran Primic fired from Bogosica Park on the 6th of December. Where did you see that in my text? Nowhere is that statement made.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question is did you place in a footnote that Zoran Primic who you're referring to and relying upon has indicated that firing did not occur from Bogosica Park on December 6th, 1991? That's all I'm asking. Did you place in a footnote that Zoran Primic, who you are relying upon, has stated that firing did not occur from Bogosica Park on 6 December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not see -- I do not see where I analysed who was doing the shooting and who participated from the Croatian firing positions on the 6th of December. We did not carry out that kind of analysis anywhere. The entire expert analysis is based on the following: If one fires from these firing positions in the counterattack, the following thing will happen. And if this does happen in the counterattack, it happens for such and such reasons. Nowhere is it stated explicitly -- I mean, I did not go into an analysis of what Primic had said or what Nojko Marinovic had said or what was stated here by Ivan Negodic before this Honourable Trial Chamber because then we would go into the following analysis, whether all of that had to be analysed generally speaking because Nojko Marinovic or rather --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you're not answering my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will pause now, Mr. Weiner. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to ask to look at the B/C/S version of the expert analysis, that is page 92. It is page 4931 in the evidence. I am going to read this footnote now. It is footnote 74. It says: "Statement by Zoran Primic".

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please slow down. It's impossible to follow at this pace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, you're ahead of the interpreters. Just go slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. "First group of mortars, 82 millimetres, DOS, on the 6th of December 1991 fired 3.000" and then there's a question mark, "mortar shells of 82 millimetres at JNA positions." So in the B/C/S version, first of all, there is this question mark. That is the first thing I wish to draw your attention to. And secondly, there is no mention of Bogosica Park. Perhaps in the process of translation and the final processing of the text, this situation that my learned friend has insisted upon actually happened. So please, look at 4931, that page. With the permission of the Honourable Trial Chamber, I would like to say another thing at this point in time. It does not have to do with this particular matter at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the core of this expert analysis fully corresponds to the methodological approach that the Prosecution expert applied in assessing the potential targets and the potential firing positions and the dispersion effects in relation to these potential targets or objectives. It is my understanding that the essence is to understand how these potential targets were decided upon. This is not evidence about whether these targets existed and whether the firing positions from which fire was opened at these targets existed. This is a series of assumptions that may or may not fit into what the facts are, before this Honourable Trial Chamber. So there is a series of targets and a series of positions. So if fire was opened from a position at a target, then there is a dispersion of a greater or lesser degree. The content of this expert report, Your Honours, is not whether there was really firing, say, from VP-1 at target number 3. This is just a group of assumptions which may be of use to the Trial Chamber if they correspond to the evidence that exists. So whether our expert got this information from Zoran Primic or from the expert opinion of Jozo Poje, that is irrelevant. It may become relevant if the expert opinion coincides with other things that the Trial Chamber heard in these proceedings. And that would be it. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. But I understand Mr. Weiner to be pursuing another point. We will resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. First, Your Honour, I have those pages, 2.364 and 65. I have ten sets, the ones that I read from the Galic case today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to show you the copy of page 5 -- actually, the whole statement of Zoran Primic which you referred to, page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, can the witness be shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, can we look at page 5, sir.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And do you see the second-full paragraph "I then directed..." Do you see that, sir? Do you see where this says that? I know you --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it. I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I just want to read it, and just tell me if I'm reading it correctly. "I then directed two of my mortars to fire on the fortress. My two mortars that fired at Srdj were located in the small soccer field behind the SDK building (I had moved them a day or two before). My other two mortar teams in Bogosica Park did not fire that day. I remained with the two mortar teams behind the SDK building." Is that what it says, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excellent. That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that's why we looked at those positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, could we move down three paragraphs where it begins, "At Ploce..." It says: "At Ploce, we collected" --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you go to the third sentence. It says: "I estimate" --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] "I continued firing..." Is it that sentence? "I estimated we fired 300 shells that day."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It doesn't say that we fired 3.000 shells, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Of course. But in Serbian translation, it is written 3.000. And I mentioned that it's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: However, sir, in your conclusion on page 88, conclusion number 7, if we want to go to your report in English, number 7 on page 88, you state: "During the attack by JNA forces on Srdj on 6 December 1991, DOS forces opened intense fire and fired around 3.000 mortar shells." And at 66, you refer to the Primic statement. In the next sentence you say: "In such conditions, it is normal that JNA mortars fired at the firing positions of DOS forces." "In such conditions," which you're referring to the intense fire of approximately 3.000 shells. And you say "in such conditions, it's normal the JNA" --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even 300 shells is intensive fire. Please. I listened to Negodic. He aimed mortars towards Srdj and his message was that he can open fire at the fort, and he was satisfied with the fact that the shells flew over the ridge and did not fall in front of the ridge of Mount Srdj. But we can't really call it a mountain. It is a hill in view of its altitude. However, firing 300 shells around the fort of Srdj is a considerable number of shells. I've told you that I learned this only later. We learned this only later. That's why I said that it was a mistake. I said that today. It's not that we intentionally used the number 3.000 shells, but in the Serbian translation of Zoran Primic's statement, it says 3.000 shells. I'm sorry I don't have this -- or rather, maybe I do. Maybe I do have it on me now, this translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you based one of your conclusions on 3.000 shells. However, if you figure 300 shells over a six-hour period, that's not intensive fire, if we talk about multiple mortars, 300 shells over a six-hour period, that's 50 mortars an hour. With multiple mortars, that's not many at all. That's not intensive fire.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 300 shells is five combat kits, so that is a large quantity. But sir, why are you overlooking the following: That in the footnotes of the final conclusions, we put a question mark in parenthesis. Why do you not take that into account? You keep ascribing this to me all the time, that I took this 3.000 almost intentionally. I did not have the English text to work from. I had the Serbian translation only. And I would finally ask the Honourable Trial Chamber to allow me to say a few words about this material that was submitted to me from the Galic trial. May I just say something in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your attorney can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No. If I would just deal with the questions put to you, Mr. Petrovic will re-examine you later. And if there's some matter there that is considered important to the Defence of General Strugar, it will be put to you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you further refer to two statements that you primarily relied on to indicate that the Old Town was not a primary target of the JNA. And you referred to, to support that, the statements of Zeljko Soldo and Nojko Marinovic, according to your report. Are you aware, sir, that both people that you relied upon, the two primary people you relied upon, Soldo and Marinovic, both indicated in their reports that the Old Town -- that the attack on the Old Town was intentional? Are you aware of that, sir, having relied upon these reports?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I'm sorry. Where was it that we wrote this? Where was it that we say that we rely on Zeljko Soldo and Nojko Marinovic's statements that there were no attacks on the Old Town? We did not mention that anywhere. Zeljko Soldo and Nojko Marinovic, their statements were only used to establish the firing positions of the Croatian forces and the JNA, nothing else. Not any assessment in terms of whether it was intentional or unintentional --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, sir, let me read again your own statement, your general conclusion on page 99. Why don't you look at it, too. In the English, it's page 99 under "General conclusion." And you state -- I'll wait until you get it.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. [In English] 99 page?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Page 99 in the English. It's under general conclusion. It says "On the basis of analysing JNA forces' actions at Dubrovnik battleground primarily on the basis of information that Prosecution witnesses Nojko Marinovic and Zeljko Soldo gave to Tribunal representatives and also in the testimony at the Tribunal by Nojko Marinovic in case IT-02-54-T of 3 April 2003 as well as other Prosecution witnesses, it cannot be concluded that fire from JNA mortars and other artillery and naval pieces was primarily directed toward Dubrovnik Old Town as its primary target." Is that what you wrote, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But sir, I beg your pardon, but you keep twisting this conclusion of ours all the time. At the very outset, we said on the basis of the testimony at the Tribunal by Nojko Marinovic and Zeljko Soldo we defined the firing positions, and that is why we invoke this here yet again because this is one of the points of departure of this analysis. We did not analyse at all anywhere, or rather there is no mention of whether this was done intentionally or unintentionally, on the basis of their statements, I mean. The expert analysis looks at the weapons and how they were fired. It does not look at the dynamics of the battle if you understand what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you indicated you based it on them. But however, let's take it a step back. Did you indicate when you mentioned those two people that both of those individuals indicated in their statements that the attack on the Old Town by the JNA on the 6th of December 1991 was an intentional act by the JNA? Did you mention that in either statement? Did you mention that in a footnote or anywhere within your report, since you're relying upon their statements?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, please, is it that you do not wish to understand what I'm saying, or is it the interpreters who are misinterpreting what I'm saying? This expert analysis did not look at witness statements at all from the aspect of whether the Old Town was targeted or not. This is a technical, ballistic analysis only, which analyses on the basis of witness statements where firing positions were and whether there could have been individual falls of individual shells into the Old Town. And I cannot give you answers to these questions of yours which go into this other kind of testimony in terms of whether somebody targeted the Old Town intentionally or unintentionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, but your report indicates that it was basically incidental, the Old Town, and that's why when you indicate that you relied upon these people, that based on your reliance of these people, there's no proof that it was intentional, that's incorrect because these people that you just mention in that same sentence as saying it was not intentional have stated that it was, in fact, intentional. Isn't that correct, sir? Let me ask you this: Are you aware that two people whose statements you have used --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, please, I think it is not fair towards General Nojko Marinovic or Zeljko Soldo to even ask the question whether they had said the Old Town had been targeted intentionally or unintentionally if it is the case that I never read a statement in that sense or used it in that sense. The data they provided was only used for determining the position of their forces and firing positions. And when I said I relied on this testimony, I meant the number and location of artillery and mortar pieces of the Croatian forces. I never read, and I'm not ascribing to General Marinovic that he denied, in fact that he didn't say that the Old Town was targeted intentionally. It wouldn't be even fair to this Honourable Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown the statement that he refers to of Zeljko Soldo, please. And also to save time, why don't we show the Marinovic statement, too. Let's look at the Zeljko Soldo statement, first.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can we look at page 7 of the Soldo statement. Sir, would you look at the second full paragraph and let me read the first two sentences and just tell me if I'm reading it correctly. "I think the attacks on Dubrovnik and the Old Town in particular came about after the attack on Srdj began to fail. There was a lot of frustration and anger among the JNA, and I think the guns were simply turned on Dubrovnik in vengeance." Is that what it says there, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did not interpret it correctly. It says here that an attack occurred on the Old Town after the attack on Srdj fell through.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I have a different translation. Could you read the second sentence, too, please.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a lot of frustration and anger among the JNA. I think that out of dissatisfaction and rage, they opened fire. Yes, that's what he says. But I was not interested in that part at all because as I said --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I just asked you --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- it was only and exclusively the first pages --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you also look at the last paragraph. And I'm going to read that along and just tell me if I'm reading it right. "The JNA took the position afterward that the shelling of Dubrovnik on 6 December 1991 was accidental or arbitrary. There was no way that this could have been the case when the battalion commander, Kovacevic, and the VPS chief of staff, Zec, were present at the forward command post at Zarkovica. From there, they had a clear perspective of what was happening, and they were clearly in control." Did I read that correctly, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, could you go to the Nojko Marinovic statement, page 21, please.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I'm even more surprised now because you just said that they had said there was no deliberate attack on Srdj on the condition that the interpretation was correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No deliberate attack -- they indicated it was a deliberate attack on the Old Town, sir. That was my question to you previously about five minutes ago. If we look at page 21, Nojko Marinovic, who you refer to, says, the first-full paragraph, first two sentences, "The three worst attacks on the Old Town occurred on 23, 24 October, 8 to 13 November, and 6 December 1991. On all three occasions, nothing had occurred on the Croatian side which justified targeting the Old Town." Is that what it says there?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what is written, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, let's go to the next paragraph. The third sentence. Actually, I'll read the paragraph, the first three sentences: "By the end of October, the JA had reached Zarkovica, the high ground southeast of the city. From there, they had an unobstructed view over the Old Town and much of Lapad. As a result, they could clearly see what they were targeting and what was being hit, particularly in the Old Town." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And just go to page 23, and that's the last one. We'll move on. If we go to page 23, the second full paragraph, it says: "All of the issues," that's how it begins. "All of these issues," I'm sorry. The third sentence: "I think the attacks on the Old Town and on other civilian targets in Dubrovnik were a sign of their desperation. They needed to break the will of the people in the city, and they were willing to suffer universal, international condemnation for a while to achieve that objective." Is that what it says there, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is written there. But may I ask you, why are you reading these conclusions to me, an expert in ballistics, asking me to confirm whether it is written there or not when I just mentioned the use of guns, and you told me that I'm not qualified to speak to these questions. It would follow that I'm not qualified to answer this either because it also goes beyond my expertise and qualification. I'm not competent or called upon to confirm witness statements or individual documents. I'm repeating to you that we only used the data about the disposition of Croatian forces and the firing positions of their weapons in making this report, including the data provided by Zeljko Soldo, excluding his comments. We made an expert report to establish whether something was possible or not, and not to confirm the claims of JNA and some of their generals about the setting of tyres on fire. The purpose of our expert analysis was not to prove that there were no deliberate attacks on the Old Town. If I had that objective in mind, I would have made a completely different analysis on how the Old Town was targeted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But nowhere in your report do you state that the persons that you rely upon, the statements that you rely upon, indicate that there was an intentional attack upon the Old Town, an intentional shelling of the Old Town. Nowhere in your report do you have a footnote or have that statement. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can I mention it? We didn't go into those statements in that way, and we didn't use them in that sense. We used them only for the narrow purpose of our analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You'll be questioned by counsel, your attorney, and you can explain. But my question to you is that nowhere --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not my lawyer, my attorney. I am an expert --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, the attorney who called you will allow you to explain some of your views. But the question I have is nowhere in your report do you state that the statements that you primarily relied on indicated that there was an intentional attack upon the Old Town. Yes or no, sir? Very simple question, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, if we had mentioned that, if we had written it in that sense, if we had written based on analysing the statement of Nojko Marinovic, we would have written, yes, the Old Town was targeted intentionally, deliberately. I cannot understand your unwillingness to accept that we used strictly that part to determine the position of JNA mortars based on Zeljko Soldo's statement and the position of Croatian forces based on Nojko Marinovic's statement. I don't see why I should have mentioned in the footnote that both Zeljko Soldo and Nojko Marinovic considered that to have been a deliberate attack. We did not view their statements in that sense from that perspective. We only used the data they provided on their pieces.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So, sir, you picked and chose within each of these statements the data you wanted to use for your report. Isn't that correct, then? You used data of Nojko Marinovic for one point; and for another point, you used information from Soldo for another point --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only technical data.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let's move on, sir. You describe in your report from pages 75 on a certain vehicle which was given the name of Charlie. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you state in conclusion number 6 on page 88 in the English: "What particularly contributed to a considerably higher number of projectiles landing in the Dubrovnik Old Town was firing from DOS artillery pieces mounted on Charlie, mobile vehicles which were fired from the northern and western sides of the walls of the Old Town." And within that, sir -- within that statement, you have a footnote indicating that the statements were from Prosecution witnesses -- statements by Prosecution witnesses Nojko Marinovic, Ivan Negodic, and Mujica Jusic, and others. Are you aware that those three individuals, those three named persons, are not witnesses at this trial or have not been witnesses at this trial? Are you aware of that, sir? I'm sorry, two of the three. We know Negodic was a witness. But Nojko Marinovic and Mujica Jusic have not been witnesses at this trial. Having monitored this case, are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Following the trial on the internet, I heard about Mujica Jusic. I heard about him, that he was in the crew of the mobile vehicle, or rather a vehicle-mounted anti-aircraft machine-gun. Ivan Negodic persistently denied that it was at all possible because he's not an expert that firing was possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, we're running out of time. We have five minutes to go today, and I'm trying to finish up as much as I can. Are you aware that two of those gentlemen, sir - sorry to interrupt you - Nojko Marinovic and Mujica Jusic were not witnesses in this trial? Are you just aware of that? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, now I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And are you also aware that those three witness statements from Ivan Negodic, Mujica Jusic, and Nojko Marinovic have never been admitted as evidence in this trial? Do you now understand that?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not aware of that. I'm hearing it from you now for the first time, all the people who were players in these events are not being taken into account at all. You are not taking into account the statements of the defenders of Dubrovnik. I'm sorry, but I find that unbelievable.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on. Also, you refer later to this in a conclusion on page 96. You refer to the Charlie vehicle again. And it says: "The fact that at least two DOS artillery pieces were mounted on lorries which changed positions after opening fire and which fired from the immediate vicinity of the Old Town walls on the western and northern sides resulted in an increased number of projectiles hitting parts of the Old Town, and particularly the part of Dubrovnik outside the Old Town, which resulted in a higher degree of destruction of this part of the town of Dubrovnik." First, is that what it states? Did I read it correctly?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you read it correctly. And below in the footnote --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Below in the footnote - we're going to get to that next - which it doesn't -- the footnote isn't represented in the text itself, but it appears to go -- obviously it goes with that paragraph. It says: "Statement by Witness Slobodan Simonovic of 20 June and 22 September, 2000 that four houses were damaged in his street because a lorry-mounted weapon had changed positions." Now, once again, having monitored this case, you are aware that Slobodan Simonovic was not a witness in this case? You know that?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know from you now. But this statement of his was present, was available just as all the previous statement of Negodic, Primic, Marinovic, and others. We had official documents through the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And these documents -- this document of Slobodan Simonovic, not only was he not here at this trial as a witness, his statement, his statement was not admitted as evidence. Are you aware of that? Or are you just learning that right now?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm learning it from you now. The only thing I heard before at the end of the examination of Prosecution witnesses, I heard that Nojko Marinovic was still not decided upon. But the moment I got some documentation through the Tribunal, I thought that it would be considered and reviewed before this Tribunal as official.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, on page 76 of your report at footnote 56, I just want to do this very briefly, you refer to a Witness Samardzic, but it pretty much contains the same information as that from Slobodan Simonovic. Are you referring to Slobodan Simonovic there? Is that just a mistake?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's an error. It's about the same person. It is the statement of Simonovic because it coincides, five houses were destroyed, and he was a member of the corps of home guards, ZNG, he was speaking about those Charlie weapons that would fire a number of rounds and then leave, and then 10 minutes later the JNA would open fire, and that's how it came about that these several houses in the vicinity of his own were destroyed. We used only that part because, in fact, Charlie existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And sir, you used only that part of Slobodan Simonovic's statement because if you look at that statement he never saw Charlie on December 6th and he never saw Charlie in any position north of the Old Town walls. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is not said explicitly the 6th of December here. The conclusions say that if fire had been opened from a certain weapon such as Charlie, mobile weapons that are in the vicinity of the Old Town, and if you remember anything within a 500-metre diameter endangers the Old Town, then it's logical that if they opened fire from locations closer to the Old Town than 500 metres, that would increase the number of projectiles that would land -- that could land into the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, we're going to have to interrupt you there. I know you're close to finishing, but that will have to be in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at 9.30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 22nd day of July, 2004, at 9.30 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.35 p.m.,
